items.title: [Bug]: Hybrid Mamba + MTP silently corrupts requests when the drafter's attention backend lowers the batch-reorder threshold (decode rows run through Mamba prefill kernels)
items.body:
## Summary

With MTP speculative decoding on a hybrid Mamba2 model (`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`), a request whose first decode step is scheduled while a long prompt is being chunk-prefilled comes back as word salad or an empty loop of special tokens for the rest of its life, from roughly its fifth token on. About 0.2–1% of requests on a mixed workload; up to 7% with a targeted trigger.

Root cause (verified with an in-process probe, see "Probe evidence"): `GPUModelRunner.calculate_reorder_batch_threshold` takes the **minimum** `reorder_batch_threshold` over all attention groups. The MTP drafter's attention backend is auto-selected independently of the target's (`llm_base_proposer.py`: "Never inherit the attention backend from base") and lands on FlashInfer, whose builder reports `1` (`supports_spec_as_decode` is false without the trtllm-gen decode kernel). The target's Mamba2 builders report `1 + k = 4`. With the runner at `1`, `reorder_batch_to_split_decodes_and_prefills` puts a 4-token draft-decode row and a chunked long prefill's *continuing chunk* in the same region and never sorts the decode rows ahead of that chunk. `Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder` then calls `split_decodes_and_prefills` at its own threshold `4`, which is positional: every row from the first prefill row on is a prefill. Decode rows behind the continuing chunk are run through `causal_conv1d_fn` / `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen`, which read and write only state slot 0 and never the `k` speculative slots. On a request's first decode step those slots have never been written; the next step's `selective_state_update` reads slot `num_accepted - 1` and the recurrent state is garbage from then on.

The docstring of `calculate_reorder_batch_threshold` says a lower threshold "just may have a performance penalty due to that backend treating decodes as prefills". That holds for token-KV attention; for backends with per-draft recurrent state it is a correctness bug.

## Environment

- vLLM 0.27.1 (both code paths unchanged on `main` at 34b9899), torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0
- 1× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120)
- Model: `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16` (NemotronH hybrid Mamba2 + attention + MoE, in-weights MTP head)

Serve command (production):

```
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16 --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 96 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --mamba-backend triton --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --async-scheduling \
  --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

Log excerpt showing the drafter picking a different backend than the target:

```
[cuda.py:422] Using AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN backend.
[gpu_model_runner.py:5332] Loading drafter model...
[cuda.py:482] Using FLASHINFER attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER', 'TRITON_ATTN'].
```

Prefix caching on (`align`) or off (`none`), `--async-scheduling` on or off, and the KV dtype make no difference. `max_num_batched_tokens` is the default 8192.

## Reproduction

Deterministic-ish trigger: keep ~30 pairs in flight, each pair = one ~60k-token prompt followed 1.5 ± 1 s later by a short (~150-token) prompt; `temperature=1.0`, `max_tokens=3000`, chat completions with `enable_thinking`. The short "follower" is admitted while the long prompt is on its 2nd–8th prefill chunk.

| variant | corrupted responses |
|---|---|
| production flags above | 15 + 2 / 400 (14 of the 200 followers); repeated on two other nodes: 12 / 400 and 9 / 400 |
| same, `--no-async-scheduling` | 14 / 400 |
| same, prefix caching off (`none` mode) | 4 / 400 (all first-step cases, as empty special-token loops) |
| same, `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536` | 6 / 400 (fewer chunked prefills, not none) |
| **no MTP** | **0 / 400** |
| **runner `reorder_batch_threshold` forced to `1 + k`** (monkeypatch) | **0 / 400**, zero misordered prefill steps in 418 |
| **drafter pinned: `"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN"` in `--speculative-config`** (its builder reports no threshold) | **0 / 400** |

A mixed workload (1 in 7 prompts 24k tokens, the rest 2.3k or short, 110 in flight, 1000 requests) reproduces at 0.2–1.6% with production flags and 0/1000 without MTP.

"Corrupted" = out-of-vocabulary word rate > 0.3 against the batch's own vocabulary, or > 200 completion tokens rendering to almost no text. Corrupted texts start with a coherent 5–15-word opener ("We are given a multiple choice question: \"") and then degenerate.

## Probe evidence

A `sitecustomize` probe (https://gist.github.com/filipmihal/ca652065fdd066063998c1bf6d3e9b8e, with the load generator and the analysis script) wrapped `GPUModelRunner._update_states`, `InputBatch.swap_states` and `Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder.build` without changing behaviour:

```
{"event": "start", "async": true, "mamba_cache_mode": "align",
 "runner_reorder_batch_threshold": 1,
 "builder_thresholds": {"Mamba2AttentionMetadataBuilder": 4, "TritonAttentionMetadataBuilder": null, "FlashInferMetadataBuilder": 1}}
```

Mamba2 prefill region of one step (`[req, num_computed_before, tokens_this_step]`): the 24k prompt's continuing chunk followed by 14 decode rows of other requests, all counted as prefills (`num_prefills = 15`):

```
[["…700f8d", 16960, 6627], ["…f9466a", 1470, 4], ["…99e300", 283, 4], ["…c17e3f", 651, 4], … ]
```

In 85 of 89 such steps the reorder recorded no swap at all (the rows were all "long_extend" at threshold 1). Across six production-flag runs with the probe, 75 of the 154 requests whose *first* decode step sat in that region were corrupted, versus 1 of 3,246 others. With the threshold forced to `1 + k`: 0 misordered steps, 0 corrupted.

With the drafter pinned to TRITON_ATTN the start line reads `"runner_reorder_batch_threshold": 4` and the FlashInfer builder is gone.

## Proposed fix

Don't let a backend that only *tolerates* a low threshold lower the threshold of a backend that *requires* ordering. PR incoming: add `requires_decode_ordering` to `AttentionMetadataBuilder` (True for the Mamba, GDN, linear-attention and short-conv builders) and have `calculate_reorder_batch_threshold` raise the minimum to the largest such builder's threshold. Attention backends already treat rows above their own threshold as prefills, so a higher global threshold costs them nothing in correctness. A more thorough fix would make the Mamba2 split independent of batch position.

Workaround for users: set `"attention_backend": "TRITON_ATTN"` (or any backend whose builder reports no threshold or `1 + k`) in `--speculative-config`, or disable MTP.

## Possibly related

- #46088 (Gemma-4 hybrid, MTP, "garbage from token 0" for short requests batched with a 64k prompt, closed "not planned") and #53180 (Qwen3.8 hybrid, MTP, intermittent degenerate output) describe the same symptom without a root cause; the mechanism above may apply if their drafter's builder reports `1`.
- #45100 (accepted-count race), #47861 / #51113 (align-mode prefix-cache snapshots) are different bugs.

items.title: [RFC] RL Test Consolidation: File Ownership, Coverage Docstrings, and CI Integration
items.body:
## Summary

This is a follow-up to **[RFC #45585: RL CI Matrix for vLLM: Behavioral + Physical + Protocol Coverage](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45585)**.

We propose keeping its three functional categories:

1. **State transitions**
2. **Information retrieval**
3. **Consistency**

The change is how those categories map to **existing test files, new tests, and CI execution**. RL-related coverage already exists in entrypoints, engines, workers, allocators, model loaders, model-specific tests, and kernels. Consolidation should account for that coverage before adding or moving suites.

Specifically:

- Keep component-level regressions next to the component they test.
- Consolidate duplicate tests at the same interface/layer.
- Use `tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/` for RL HTTP contracts and cross-component lifecycle tests.
- Document category scope and existing coverage locations in the **`rlhf/__init__.py` module docstring**, and explain each test module's contract and boundaries in its own **module docstring**. No new test README is proposed.
- Give each test/configuration an explicit CI execution owner, with appropriate GPU count, backend, and platform selection.
- Amend the existing PRs rather than replacing them with a new umbrella implementation PR.

This issue proposes the reorganization; the file moves, test changes, and CI changes below are not implemented by opening this RFC.

## Relationship to existing RFCs

#45585 remains the umbrella motivation and behavioral/physical/protocol coverage framework. This proposal revises its blanket migration approach and updates the implementation plan against coverage that has since landed.

It does not replace the product contracts in the related RFCs:

- #48311 — Engine Sleep/Wake/Drain Lifecycle for RL
- #48310 — Sleep/Wake Correctness for RL
- #48312 — Weight Reload Correctness for RL
- #48306 — RL Information Retrieval: APIs & Introspection
- #42259 — Logprobs/Logits Semantics and Determinism
- #51476 — DP pause/sleep correctness and layering

Those RFCs define the relevant semantics. This issue defines where their regression coverage belongs, how the current test PRs should be adjusted, and how CI should execute it. Proposed semantics must not be treated as already implemented contracts.

## Why revisit the file mapping?

The original breakdown was largely one topic/file/PR at a time. The broad categories still make sense, but the repository now has overlapping coverage at different layers.

Examples:

- `test_mem.py` covers more than allocator flags: it includes CUDA graphs, offline sleep/reload, LoRA, async deep sleep, and FP8 KV cache.
- `test_weight_transfer_llm.py` uses a mock transfer engine to test the LLM API contract; it does not replace real IPC/NCCL transfer tests.
- `test_reload.py` already changes checkpoints and checks their effect, including quantized and distributed configurations.
- Engine and DP suites already cover pause/resume, late requests, drain, and race/deadlock regressions.
- Routed-experts tests exist at frontend, model-executor, and kernel layers.

Moving every one of these into an HTTP test directory would obscure ownership. Adding a new HTTP test for every existing lower-level case would increase cost without necessarily adding useful coverage.

The inventory below is based on a repository source audit and targeted upstream-main checks. It is a coverage inventory, **not a claim that every listed configuration currently passes CI**.

## Current PR status

Snapshot at filing (2026-09-05). Short head SHAs identify the versions inspected; PR bodies and historical test results may describe earlier revisions.

| Area | PR | Status | Inspected head | Current scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sleep/wake | #54930 | Open, draft | `c573143585ce` | HTTP sleep/wake suite parameterized over MRV1/MRV2 |
| Pause/resume | #52144 | Merged | `bf2c4252763e` | HTTP pause modes, request lifecycle, idempotency, validation, cache behavior |
| Weight update + metrics | #53541 | Open, non-draft | `accc4d3f0e1c` | Transfer tests, reload smoke, metrics, and new frontend state/version machinery |
| Weight checker | #51350 | Open, non-draft | `7252f6670c65` | Checksum/reset/compare feature and tests, including distributed reload verification |
| Response schema + weight info | #52864 | Open, non-draft | `8314de984014` | Structured sleep responses and current weight-version HTTP contract |
| Routed experts | #52902 | Open, draft | `df0f2194f653` | Latest diff: TP2×DP2 token-in/token-out capture and reduced-model OpenAI frontend coverage |
| CPU lifecycle-state coverage | No dedicated PR in this breakdown | Proposed gap audit | — | Extend production-module tests after subtracting existing engine/worker/DP coverage |

## Proposed ownership rules

1. **Place tests near their direct subject.** Allocator, worker, loader, and kernel invariants normally stay in their component suites.
2. **Merge duplication within a layer.** Two HTTP tests checking the same endpoint behavior are candidates for consolidation. A worker error-path test and an HTTP lifecycle test can be complementary.
3. **Review mixed files by test group.** A file containing allocator and offline-LLM cases must not be moved wholesale based on its name.
4. **Preserve execution coverage when moving tests.** Preserve frontend variants, eager/graph coverage, supported platforms, and resource requirements.
5. **Test the production state owner.** Do not create an independent test-only state machine just to populate a planned file.
6. **Use the cheapest effective level.** Exhaustive input validation and local invariants belong in unit tests; retain a small E2E set for actual cross-layer behavior.

### Existing coverage and proposed disposition

All paths below are repository-relative. “Keep” means retain the test's primary implementation location and reference it from the RL coverage docstrings.

| Category | Existing file | Coverage | Proposed disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| State transitions | `tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/test_sleep.py` | HTTP flags, metrics, staged wake | Merge into `rlhf/state_transitions/test_sleep_wake.py`; remove old file only after coverage parity |
| State transitions | `tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/state_transitions/test_pause_resume.py` | HTTP pause/resume contract | Keep |
| State transitions | `tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm.py` | Engine pause modes, queued cancellation, multiple requests | Keep; avoid duplicating its complete matrix at HTTP level |
| State transitions | `tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py` | DP/EP pause, late requests/drain, staggered ranks, barrier regressions; upstream also has wait/device-idle cases | Keep in distributed CI; reference exact relevant test functions |
| State transitions | `tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py` | Backend factory, capabilities, backend state | Keep; this is not engine lifecycle-state coverage |
| State transitions | `tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py` | Allocator/discard/graph and offline sleep/reload | Keep initially; any later split separates allocator from offline-LLM groups and preserves assertions |
| State transitions | `tests/models/language/generation/test_gdn_sleep_wake.py` | Hybrid state-cache regression after wake | Keep model-specific ownership and hybrid-model selection |
| State transitions | `tests/entrypoints/weight_transfer/test_weight_transfer_llm.py` | LLM API delegation through mock transport, version behavior | Keep |
| State transitions | `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker_weight_transfer.py` | Session guards, delegation, error cleanup | Keep and extend only for missing behavior |
| State transitions | `tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py` | IPC/NCCL/sparse transport, trainer/client, metadata validation | Keep |
| State transitions | `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py` | Actual A/B checkpoint reload, quantization, KV scales, aliases/buffers/storage | Keep and extend here instead of duplicating weaker reload tests |
| Consistency | `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_return_routed_experts.py` | OpenAI frontend capture response | Retain lightweight frontend smoke; share validation helpers if useful |
| Consistency | `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_return_routed_experts.py` | Token-in/token-out capture response | Retain single-GPU smoke; add multi-GPU coverage separately |
| Consistency | `tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py` | EPLB/DP/TP capture, MRV2 output, KV-group selection | Keep |
| Consistency | `tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_experts_capture_monolithic.py` | Backend-specific BF16/FP8/NVFP4 capture | Keep in supported-hardware kernel jobs |
| Consistency | `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py`, `test_logprobs_e2e.py`, and `tests/v1/determinism/` | General logprobs/determinism | Keep; RL adds lifecycle-specific checks only |

Frontend routed-experts smoke may instead be physically consolidated if maintainers prefer. The acceptance condition is unchanged: preserve the independently runnable frontend contracts, remove duplicate copies, and update CI ownership. This RFC's default is to keep them near their frontends.

## Coverage documentation through docstrings

### Package docstring

Add a concise, documentation-only `tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/__init__.py` describing:

- The three categories and their behavioral scope.
- RL HTTP/lifecycle modules maintained under this package.
- Existing component coverage outside this package, with repository-relative paths and representative function/class names.
- The distinction between local coverage and referenced coverage.
- Links to #45585 and this follow-up RFC.

It must not import the referenced suites, initialize GPU dependencies, or change test collection.

### Test-module docstrings

Each affected test module should explain:

- The production interface/contract it tests.
- The observable failure or regression it guards.
- Important coverage already owned by another test module.
- Non-obvious execution requirements or matrix boundaries.

For example, the sleep/wake module could document the following intended boundary:

```python
"""HTTP sleep/wake lifecycle coverage for RL rollout.

Checks request gating during partial wake and successful generation after
memory and weights are restored. Resource-only and long-cycle cases are
selected separately from the small lifecycle smoke suite.

Related coverage:
    tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py: allocator and offline sleep/reload.
    tests/v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py: DP pause/drain regressions.
    tests/models/language/generation/test_gdn_sleep_wake.py: hybrid state cache.
"""
```

The final wording must describe assertions actually implemented by the module.

Keep volatile PR status and outstanding work in this RFC, rather than embedding “done” claims in Python files. Docstrings record stable scope and ownership; CI configuration remains authoritative for execution. Update affected cross-references in the same change as a move or rename. No symlinks, wrapper imports, or new README are needed.

## Target RL HTTP/lifecycle modules

Under `tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/`:

| Subpackage | Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Package | `__init__.py` | Category scope and coverage-location index |
| Package | `conftest.py` | Shared fixtures and narrowly reusable HTTP/lifecycle helpers |
| State transitions | `test_pause_resume.py` | Existing minimal HTTP request-lifecycle contract |
| State transitions | `test_sleep_wake.py` | HTTP gating, staged/full wake, restored generation |
| State transitions | `test_weight_update.py` | Configured real transfer, error contract, version/cache effects |
| State transitions | `test_weight_update_metrics.py` | Actual transaction metrics, after metric semantics are agreed |
| State transitions | `test_weight_checker.py` | Checker API and corruption/recovery verification |
| State transitions | `test_rl_step.py` (proposed) | Small compound lifecycle across interfaces |
| Information retrieval | `test_response_schema.py` | Response fields/types and rejected-input behavior |
| Information retrieval | `test_weight_info.py` | Current `weight_version` query/update contract |
| Consistency | `test_routed_experts.py` | Lifecycle/cache-related routing correctness beyond frontend smoke |

CPU engine-state tests should extend nearby engine suites, or use a narrowly scoped engine test module if no existing suite fits. Worker session tests remain in the existing worker module. We do not require the original `rlhf/test_state_machine*.py` layout.

## Planned changes to existing PRs

### #54930 — Sleep/wake

- Move the suite to `state_transitions/` and consolidate the old HTTP sleep test with explicit coverage parity.
- Replace “request was not successful” checks with precise pending/rejected/completed semantics.
- For partial wake, observe that the **same request** does not complete prematurely and does complete after full wake; propagate background exceptions and join all threads.
- Cover both tag orders where supported. A fresh successful request after wake is not sufficient to prove the earlier request survived.
- Separate level-2 flag/resource checks from recovery tests. A level-2 recovery test must restore weights before generation; a shared fixture cannot treat wake alone as weight restoration.
- Verify cache effects directly, rather than only checking that a repeated prompt generates.
- Merge redundant flag/cycle cases; keep representative runner and graph coverage.
- Separate long-cycle resource checks from smoke. Put dedicated performance benchmarks under the benchmark infrastructure rather than making general CI depend on machine-specific latency limits.
- Use exact idempotency/error contracts instead of accepting unrelated status codes such as both 200 and 400.

### #52144 — Pause/resume

Keep the merged suite and its focused contract. Amend helpers only through a coordinated infrastructure change.

Changes motivated by #51476 should track the relevant implementation contract. Do not change admission expectations solely because a proposed semantic change exists. Also distinguish engine completion from the client's receipt of the final streaming chunk when synchronizing assertions.

### #53541 — Weight update and metrics

Separate the test increment from product-design changes:

1. Real HTTP transfer and protocol tests.
2. Metrics implementation/semantics and associated tests.
3. Any additional state-management feature, only after demonstrating a gap in the existing engine/worker ownership.

Required test changes:

- Success tests use a configured/initialized backend and require success; HTTP 500 is not a successful protocol outcome.
- Invalid-order tests have explicit expected responses and state-preservation/recovery checks.
- Provide deterministic compatible A/B weights in CI. Core transfer coverage must not silently disappear because `VLLM_TEST_MODEL_ALT` is unset.
- Compare warm-updated B with a B reference, or another controlled numerical oracle; “text changed” alone does not establish correct transfer.
- Warm the relevant cache under A, update to B, and verify cache coherence and B results.
- Remove or relocate the reload smoke that only calls initialize/finalize without loading replacement weights. Reuse `test_reload.py` for actual model/quantization reload coverage.
- Exercise real metric transitions: active 0→1→0, successful counter increments, histogram observation count, and the agreed failure behavior.
- Define multi-API-process and DP metric/state ownership; frontend-local state and a fixed engine label need explicit justification.

There is also a cross-PR contract conflict: #52864 tests the existing `weight_version` response, while #53541 introduces `weight_gen/weight_label` and expands `/weight_info`. Resolve the API design first. Weakening schema tests to accept both is not the resolution. This proposal defaults to the upstream `weight_version` contract; any additional counter has separate semantics.

### #51350 — Weight checker

Keep this as a feature PR with its own focused tests.

- Align documentation and tests with the latest checksum/reset/compare baseline lifecycle, including compare's one-shot behavior.
- Ensure tests independently establish/consume their baseline and restore mutated weights.
- Use small unit tests for supported tensor types, hashing/coverage policy, and key merging.
- Verify the complete rank-qualified key inventory and negative cases such as missing ranks/tensors or changed values.
- Retain distributed reset→reload→compare; add real-transfer restoration as a distinct integration path.
- Schedule TP2×DP2×EP on an explicitly provisioned four-GPU job.

### #52864 — Schema and weight information

Keep the current scope. Use router-level CPU tests with a fake engine client for exhaustive field/input validation where practical, plus a small real-engine E2E set.

A schema matrix does not need to multiply every case by runner and parallelism. Successful transfer's version-commit behavior belongs in weight-update/compound lifecycle coverage.

### #52902 — Routed experts

Reconcile the PR description and reported results with the latest diff before expanding it.

The inspected version primarily checks capture shape/range across frontends/models and TP2×DP2. That should not be described as complete routing-replay correctness.

- Preserve cheap single-GPU frontend smoke when adding distributed/model cases.
- Add exact token/row alignment, cache-hit recovery, mixed-batch isolation, and lifecycle-related stale-routing checks.
- Shape/range alone cannot detect a valid-range all-zero capture; use a controlled/reference routing oracle where applicable.
- Repeated deterministic generation is not a test of consuming captured routes for replay. Add actual replay validation only through an available supported path; otherwise track it as a gap.
- Keep backend-specific checks near kernel tests and explicitly select supported hardware.
- Reduced-geometry dummy models establish code-path coverage, not real-checkpoint numerical correctness.
- Preserve graph coverage explicitly; a shared harness that forces eager cannot establish graph behavior.

### Shared infrastructure

Resolve the differing `server()` signatures/defaults across these PRs in one coordinated change. Prefer the repository's existing server utilities where they fit. Make model, environment, sleep enablement, execution mode, port handling, logging, and process cleanup explicit.

Do not collapse transport exceptions into a generic unsuccessful response for behavioral assertions. Reuse servers only when state is restored reliably; destructive weight changes need restoration or isolation.

## CI integration

Keep the three functional categories, and split execution within them by cost and resource requirements.

| Execution group | Scope | Resource policy |
|---|---|---|
| CPU/unit | Router contracts, actual engine/worker invariants, checker small-tensor behavior | Verify collection and execution without GPU dependencies |
| State transitions smoke | Core pause/sleep behavior, real IPC, minimal compound step | One GPU where topology permits; critical MRV1/MRV2 compatibility paths |
| Information retrieval smoke | Schema/version; small real-engine cross-check | CPU plus a small one-GPU E2E subset |
| Consistency smoke | Small-MoE capture/alignment and lifecycle correctness | One GPU, selected eager/graph scenarios |
| Distributed | NCCL, TP, DP/EP, rank completeness | Explicit two/four-GPU topology, including trainer resources |
| Hardware/extended | Supported quantization/kernel paths, long cycles, larger models | Dedicated hardware and explicit optional/scheduled selection |

Operational requirements:

- The existing entrypoints API-server job recursively collects `entrypoints/serve`. Its upstream four-way sharding does not provide four GPUs to an individual test.
- If dedicated RL jobs take ownership, exclude those tests from the former recursive job in the same change, including applicable AMD mirrors.
- Existing component jobs should remain the primary owners of their suites. The RL docstrings reference them without causing duplicate collection.
- Update source-file dependencies as well as pytest commands when moving tests.
- Use supported markers and explicit job selection. Adding a `nightly` marker alone does not schedule a job.
- Record passed, skipped, and deselected configurations separately. An advertised critical lane that skips its only transfer/hardware case is not established coverage.
- Avoid a full model × runner × backend × parallelism Cartesian product. Select combinations that exercise materially different paths.

## Remaining implementation work and order

- [ ] Agree on the file-ownership table and the docstring-based coverage index.
- [ ] Coordinate shared harness changes across the open PRs.
- [ ] Amend #54930 and consolidate the old HTTP sleep test without losing coverage.
- [ ] Separate and strengthen #53541; resolve version/metrics/state ownership with #52864.
- [ ] Audit CPU lifecycle gaps against existing engine, worker, and upstream DP tests; add only missing production behavior.
- [ ] Add a minimal complete RL-step test, then two consecutive steps.
- [ ] Complete #51350's checker contract and assign its distributed execution lane.
- [ ] Amend #52902 with precise capture-versus-replay scope and preserve frontend smoke.
- [ ] Add or reuse physical edge-case regressions after checking prior work in #45585.
- [ ] Wire CI ownership/resource selection and verify collection after every migration.
- [ ] Extend model/backend-specific coverage only where the inventory identifies an uncovered path.

A representative level-2 compound step is:

```text
rollout with A
→ pause/quiesce according to the implemented contract
→ sleep(level=2)
→ wake(weights)
→ transfer B and finish(weight_version=B)
→ wake(kv_cache), restore scheduling as required
→ rollout and compare with B reference
→ repeat for the next version
```

Assert request liveness, restored output/logprobs, committed version, and cache coherence. Metrics/checker assertions can be added as their features land; they need not block the initial compound test.

Coordinate physical tests with the earlier contributions linked in #45585. Its discussion also contains ownership of parallel-sampling abort-count/parent-child cleanup work; this reorganization should not duplicate that feature work.

## Acceptance criteria and feedback requested

Consolidation is complete when:

- Every claimed behavior has an identifiable test implementation and CI execution path.
- File moves preserve relevant platforms, frontends, and execution modes.
- Same-layer duplicates are removed; complementary component tests remain discoverable.
- Package and module docstrings describe implemented scope and point to existing coverage.
- Core real-transfer and lifecycle tests run in their designated lanes with meaningful oracles.
- PR descriptions match the current diff and separate source-audited coverage from actually executed validation.

Feedback requested: agreement on the ownership/migration table, frontend routed-experts placement, and resource-based CI partitioning before implementing the reorganization.

**Validation for this RFC:** source/diff review and targeted upstream-main/CI inspection only. No code changes or GPU test runs are claimed.

items.title: [Bug]: thinking_token_budget ignored by Model Runner V2 with Qwen3.8 NVFP4 + MTP
items.body:
## Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text Collecting environment information... items.title: [Bugfix] Name the real cause when a TurboQuant layer resolves to "auto"
items.body:
## Summary

A hybrid model (linear-attention / state layers alongside full-attention ones) started with `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_*` fails at engine init with:

```
ValueError: Unknown TurboQuant cache dtype: 'auto'.
Valid presets: turboquant_k8v4, turboquant_4bit_nc, turboquant_k3v4_nc, turboquant_3bit_nc
```

`auto` is not a preset the user typed, and it is not something they can fix by picking a different value from that list — it means a layer is not TurboQuant-compressible. The message sends them looking in the wrong place.

This reports that instead, and says what to do about it.

Fixes #53334 (observation 1).

## A question for maintainers

This assumes hybrid models are **intentionally** out of scope for the TurboQuant KV cache, and so treats the failure as a message problem.

The reporter framed it as a fork: *"If hybrids are intended to be unsupported, a clearer message would fail earlier and clearer; if support is intended, this is the blocker."*

I do not know which is the case. If hybrid support is planned, this is the wrong fix — please close it and treat #53334 observation 1 as a feature blocker rather than a UX issue.

## Test

`tests/quantization/test_turboquant.py::TestTurboQuantConfig::test_auto_state_layer_dtype_raises_actionable` asserts the message no longer reports `auto` as an unknown preset and names the real cause. Verified against `main` (old message) and with this change (new message).

items.title: [Model]: GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next): no sparse-MLA attention path on Ada (sm_89, RTX 4090)
items.body:
### Environment

- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (Ada, compute capability 8.9, 48 GiB each)
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash-cu129` (vLLM `0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187`, built from PR #53906)
- Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8 checkpoint, `model_type=glm5_next`, `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`)
- Launch: TP=8, local weights, `--reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47`

### What happens

Workers fail during `load_model` at attention backend selection. No backend accepts this model's sparse MLA configuration on sm_89:

```
ValueError: No valid attention backend found for cuda with
AttentionSelectorConfig(head_size=512, dtype=torch.bfloat16,
kv_cache_dtype=auto, block_size=None, use_mla=True, has_sink=False,
use_sparse=True, use_mm_prefix=False, use_per_head_quant_scales=False,
attn_type=AttentionType.DECODER, has_sliding_window=False,
use_non_causal=False, use_batch_invariant=False, use_kv_connector=True,
use_adaptive_verification=False, use_pcp=False).
Reasons: {
  FLASH_ATTN_MLA: [sparse not supported, compute capability not supported, FlashAttention MLA not supported on this device],
  FLASHMLA: [sparse not supported, compute capability not supported, FlashMLA Sparse is only supported on Hopper and Blackwell DC devices.],
  FLASHINFER_MLA: [sparse not supported, compute capability not supported, FlashInfer MLA kernel requires qk_nope_head_dim in [64, 128, 192], but got 256],
  TRITON_MLA: [sparse not supported],
  FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90: [compute capability not supported, requires SM90 + FlashInfer >= 0.6.18],
  FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE: [compute capability not supported, FlashAttention MLA not supported on this device],
  FLASHMLA_SPARSE: [compute capability not supported]
}
```

### What works on the same GPUs

- Weight loading is clean (native FP8 checkpoint, 62 shards, ~306 GiB).
- torch (`2.13.0+cu129`) CUDA compute works on sm_89; Triton compiles and detects `arch=89`.
- Full engine config validation passes (TP=8, KV offload, prefix caching). The failure is specifically the sparse-MLA attention lane: rope-free MLA (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`) + `head_dim=256` + sparse indexer.

### Context

- The recipe page states the implementation supports "NVIDIA Hopper and newer", so this may be intentional; filing to confirm and to register demand.
- SM120 (RTX PRO 6000) has the same class of gap: #53963. So currently only SM90/SM100 appear to work.
- For reference, sparse-MLA variants for DeepSeek-style models have been made to run on sm_89 via community/custom FlashInfer builds, so Ada silicon is capable of this class of kernel — GLM-5.3's rope-free variant (head_dim 256) just has no implementation path wired up for it yet.

### Ask

1. Is an sm_89 (Ada) sparse-MLA path planned or considered in scope for the GLM-5.3 integration (PR #53906)?
2. If not planned, would a contribution adding an sm_89 path (or a Triton fallback for the sparse MLA indexer + decode path) be welcome? Any guidance on which backend to extend (FlashInfer vs Triton) would help.
3. If Ada is officially out of scope, a one-line note in the recipe/docs ("Ada/sm_89 unsupported") would save others the bring-up attempt.

items.title: [Spec Decode][ROCm] Add FLy: entropy-gated deferred verification for draft-model speculative decoding

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Run pre-commit for new contributors without triggering other tests

items.body:
## Purpose

This PR adds **FLy** ([arXiv:2511.22972](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.22972)) (Accepted by ICLR 2026), an opt-in verification policy for draft-model speculative decoding, developed and evaluated at **AMD**.

Standard rejection sampling stops at the first rejected draft token, so a single ambiguous position truncates the whole draft and discards the tokens the target has already verified. FLy observes that when the *following* acceptance decisions all still agree, an isolated rejection at a genuinely ambiguous position is usually not worth a full truncation. At such a position, FLy defers to the draft token instead of rejecting, which lets the rest of the window be accepted.

Evaluated over 40 model–dataset configurations, covering four target/draft pairs across ten benchmarks. The pairs include a 405B FP8 model and a 235B MoE reasoning model, and an independent NVIDIA validation is included as well. FLy is faster than standard speculative decoding in every configuration.

## Executive Summary

We completed an end-to-end evaluation of FLy against target-only decoding and standard speculative decoding (Standard SD). The AMD MI355X evaluation is the primary result set and covers four target/draft model pairs across 10 benchmarks, for a total of 40 model–dataset configurations.

- **Consistent acceleration on AMD:** FLy is faster than Standard SD in all 40 primary configurations, with speedups from **1.067x to 1.938x**. The typical improvement is about **1.23x**.
- **Quality preservation on AMD:** among the 29 configurations for which a quality-retention ratio is reported, the minimum retention is **97.9%**. **23** configurations exceed 99%. Low-correct-count AIME/HLE cases report the three raw correct counts instead of a ratio.
- **Mechanistic improvement:** draft acceptance and mean accepted tokens per verification round (`tau`) increase in every AMD primary row. The `tau` improvement ranges from **1.03x to 1.83x**.
- **Surpass the state-of-the-art method: on the MI300x, FLy surpasses DFlash by over 1.09x** on the Kimi-K2.5-1T model with 8k/1k input/output sequence length while keeping 99.7% of the GSM8k accuracy.
- **Cross-platform validation:** on the NVIDIA B300 evaluation, FLy improves over Standard SD on all 7 listed workloads, by **1.07x to 1.43x**.
- **Sampling-path coverage:** Supplementary experiments on AMD and NVIDIA further validate FLy beyond the default temperature-0 setting, covering non-zero-temperature decoding under two speculative sampling policies: greedy drafting with target-only verification, and probabilistic drafting with standard p/q rejection sampling.

## Mechanism

FLy lives entirely in the verification/sampling stage. After the target model has produced logits for the drafted positions, `RejectionSampler.rejection_sample()` normally runs one of two native acceptance kernels; FLy inserts a single pre-pass in front of them that can flip individual *rejections* into acceptances at high-entropy positions, after which the native kernels run unmodified. Nothing in drafting, scheduling, KV cache, attention, or the model runner is touched, and no extra checkpoint or confidence head is required.

```text
draft model proposes K tokens
        │
target model forward  ──►  target_logits for the K drafted positions
        │
        ▼
  RejectionSampler.rejection_sample()          ← the only place FLy touches
        │
        ├── [FLy pre-pass]  top-3 target entropy, then at gated positions only:
        │       greedy path :  target_argmax[i] <- draft_token_ids[i]
        │       random path :  uniform_probs[i] <- 0
        │
        └── native rejection_{greedy,random}_sample_kernel   (unmodified)
                │
                ▼
        accepted tokens + bonus token
```

The pre-pass does not re-implement acceptance; it rewrites the *inputs* the native kernels read, so the unchanged native logic emits the deferred decision. Overwriting the target argmax makes the native equality test pass on the greedy path, and setting the uniform sample to `0` makes the native `p/q >= u` test pass on the random path once `p > 0` and `q > 0` are checked. Per-position accounting and acceptance metrics therefore stay on the existing code path.

A native rejection at position `i` is overridden only if all of the following hold:

| Gate condition | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| target top-3 entropy at `i` >= `fly_entropy_threshold` | the target is genuinely uncertain here, not confidently disagreeing |
| the next `fly_window_size` positions would all be accepted natively | the draft has re-synchronised, so the deferral is local |
| the draft token has non-zero target probability | never emit a token the target assigns zero mass |
| `i + fly_window_size < num_draft_tokens` | a full window must fit in the remaining draft |

The entropy is computed from the target scores *after* temperature, top-k, and top-p processing, so the gate reflects the distribution actually being sampled from. When FLy is disabled, no entropy is computed, neither pre-pass kernel is launched, and the code path is exactly the pre-existing one.

Because the pre-pass reads only `target_logits` and the proposed token IDs, FLy is independent of *how* the draft was produced. It is therefore enabled both for `draft_model` drafting and for the hidden-state drafting methods (`eagle`, `eagle3`, `mtp`, `dflash`, `dspark`), including their parallel drafting: a parallel drafter still proposes a linear token sequence, and the target logits at each position are still conditioned on the proposed token before it. FLy composes with those methods rather than competing with them.

## Usage

```python
llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
    speculative_config={
        "method": "draft_model",
        "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 8,
        "rejection_sample_method": "fly",
        "fly_window_size": 6,          # default 6, must be < num_speculative_tokens
        "fly_entropy_threshold": 0.3,  # default 0.3
    },
)
```

FLy is disabled by default. Config validation rejects unsupported combinations up front: it requires a trained drafter (`draft_model` or one of the hidden-state methods above), a shared target/draft vocabulary, and `fly_window_size < num_speculative_tokens`. It works with both the default target-only acceptance and `draft_sample_method="probabilistic"`.

The pre-pass is implemented in the V1 model runner's rejection sampler, so FLy is V1-only for now: configurations that merely *default* to V2 fall back to V1 with a warning when FLy is enabled, and configurations that *require* V2 are rejected with an explicit error rather than silently ignoring the flag. See [Limitations](#limitations).

## Evaluation

### Setup

All primary results run on **AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950)** with torch.compile and HIP graph enabled, at temperature 0 with greedy drafting and target-only verification. The evaluation covers `draft_model` drafting; the hidden-state drafting methods are supported by the same code path but are not measured here.

| Target / draft | `num_speculative_tokens` | TP | Concurrency |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct / Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 15 | 1 | 32 |
| DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B / 8B | 15 | 1 | 32 |
| Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-FP8-KV / Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 25 | 2 | 32 |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507-FP8 / Qwen3-8B | 15 | 2 | 16 |

Standard SD and FLy differ by exactly one setting, `rejection_sample_method` (`"standard"` vs `"fly"`). The draft checkpoint, `num_speculative_tokens`, torch.compile and graph-capture settings, sampling parameters and the V1 draft-model proposer path are identical, so both configurations have identical prerequisites.

`T` / `SD` / `FLy` denote target-only decoding, standard speculative decoding and FLy. Throughput is generated output tokens per second, draft acceptance excludes bonus tokens, and `tau = 1 + accepted draft tokens / verification rounds`. Retention is FLy accuracy divided by the lower of Target and Standard SD, since Standard SD itself sometimes lands below Target on greedy tie-breaks. Every row states its own concurrency (`BS`). Spec-Bench quality is measured on its 80-question math subset while throughput uses the full 480-prompt workload.

## Limitations

1. **FLy is an approximate verification policy.** It does not preserve the target distribution exactly, so it is opt-in and nothing changes unless `rejection_sample_method="fly"` is set. Across the 40 configurations above the measured cost is small: retention is at least 97.9% wherever a ratio is reported.

2. **Three of the eleven raw-count configurations where FLy is below both Target and Standard SD.** All three are benchmarks on which even the target model answers very few questions correctly, so a difference of one to three questions dominates2:

   | Target / draft | Dataset | T / SD / FLy correct | Total |
   | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
   | DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B / 8B | AIME 2024 | 20 / 20 / 17 | 30 |
   | DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B / 8B | HLE | 4 / 4 / 3 | 64 |
   | Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507-FP8 / Qwen3-8B | HLE | 11 / 11 / 8 | 64 |

   These are excluded from the 97.9% retention floor quoted above, which covers the 29 configurations that report a ratio.

3. **V1 model runner only, for now.** FLy is implemented in the V1 rejection sampler. The evaluation above uses draft-model speculative decoding with a separate draft and target model, which the V2 model runner does not support, so V1 is the runner for this setup in any case. For hidden-state drafting, enabling FLy makes the engine fall back to V1 with a warning; configurations that require V2, such as `dspark`, are rejected rather than silently ignoring the flag. Adapting FLy to the V2 sampler is planned as follow-up work.

## Why this is not a duplicate

Several concurrent PRs touch the verification step, but they change *how many* draft tokens are verified, while FLy changes *the accept/reject decision itself*:

- [#47808](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47808) (DSpark confidence-scheduled verification) and [#47131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47131) (D-Cut) size or prune the verification budget from draft confidence *before* verification and leave the acceptance test intact. FLy leaves the budget alone and overrides individual rejections instead, so the two are complementary.
- [#50246](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50246) proposes **DFly**, which despite the similar name is a drafting method rather than a verification policy.

As of this submission, I found no other PR that modifies the acceptance decision itself in `rejection_sampler.py`.

## Drive-by doc fix

The `rejection_sample_method` row in the speculative decoding docs was stale: it listed a non-existent `strict` default, omitted `block`, and listed `probabilistic`, which belongs to `draft_sample_method`. This PR corrects that row and adds the missing `draft_sample_method` row, which `use_heterogeneous_vocab` right below it already referenced.

## Test Plan / Test Result

```bash
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py -k fly   # 6 passed
pytest tests/test_config.py -k fly                        # 10 passed
```

The new cases cover the greedy and random deferral paths, the entropy gate, window boundary conditions, the accepted drafting methods, and rejection of invalid configs; the full rejection-sampler suite (81 tests) passes unchanged. End-to-end results are the tables above. The change is pure Python and the Triton kernels JIT-compile unmodified on both ROCm and CUDA, so no kernel rebuild is needed on either platform.

## Attribution

This work was done at **AMD** and the primary evaluation ran on AMD Instinct MI355X. AI assistance was used for this change (recorded as `Assisted-by:` in the commit trailer). I have reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations above myself.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Fail requests the KV cache pool can never hold instead of retrying them forever
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52520.

### The symptom

On a hybrid Mamba + full-attention model with `--mamba-cache-mode align`, a request
whose length is near the KV pool ceiling is **accepted**, chunk-prefilled to ~99 % of
the pool, descheduled when the last chunk cannot be allocated — and then never
scheduled again. Zero output tokens, the whole prefill discarded, and the only
observable is `vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason{reason="capacity"} = 1`, which is
indistinguishable from a healthy server that is momentarily full. The HTTP request
never returns.

The engine boots happily into this state: `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` passes.

### The mechanism

Two bounds describe the same quantity — how many blocks one `max_model_len` request
can hold at once — and they are computed by different code that does not agree.

**Startup** sizes the pool from each spec's `max_memory_usage_bytes`
(`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:2189-2198`). For a hybrid Mamba model in align mode
that is `cdiv(max_model_len, block_size)` blocks for the attention group plus
`2 + num_speculative_blocks` for the Mamba group
(`vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:687-696`). It compares that against **all** the
blocks the pool will have. But `BlockPool` permanently reserves one block as the null
block (`vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py:188-191`), so only `num_blocks - 1` are ever
available to a request. A pool built at exactly the startup minimum is one usable
block short of one `max_model_len` request, and startup does not notice.

**Runtime admission** (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:475-491`, reached with
`scheduler_reserve_full_isl` — default `True`) asks the coordinator for the same
quantity, but through the per-step allocators. For the Mamba align group that path
returns `1 + num_speculative_blocks` on a first prefill
(`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1529-1540`), one block below the peak
the spec itself states, because a later step allocates the next state block before
`remove_skipped_blocks` retires the one from two steps ago. So admission asks for one
block *less* than the pool is short by, and admits.

The request then chunk-prefills until the final chunk needs the block that does not
exist. It is the only running request, so it preempts itself
(`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:676-688`): `num_computed_tokens` back to 0, all
blocks freed, requeued. On the next step the same gate now also has to count the
blocks the discarded prefill left in the prefix cache as evictable, so it refuses —
and keeps refusing. The request is stuck, and the prefill is gone.

Measured on unmodified `main` at `4d2a68d64d9e05921ed5c4099146e768a92d71d5`, CPU only,
no model weights: hybrid full-attention + Mamba(align), `block_size=16`,
`max_model_len=1024`, `num_speculative_blocks=3`, `max_num_batched_tokens=256`. The
startup bound is `cdiv(1024,16)=64 + (2+3)=5 = 69` blocks, and
`get_kv_cache_configs` accepts a 69-block pool:

```text
pool of 69 blocks: startup check accepts=True (num_blocks=69)
  pool=69 blocks, free at start=68 (one block is BlockPool's null block)
    step   0 scheduled=  256 computed=  256 free= 48 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
    step   1 scheduled=  256 computed=  512 free= 31 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
    step   2 scheduled=  256 computed=  768 free= 15 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
    step   3 scheduled=  240 computed= 1008 free=  0 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
    step   4 scheduled=    0 computed=    0 free= 68 status=PREEMPTED preemptions=1
    step   5 scheduled=    0 computed=    0 free= 68 status=PREEMPTED preemptions=1
    ... 19 more identical steps ...
  VERDICT prompt=1023: finished=False computed=0 preemptions=1 status=PREEMPTED

pool of 70 blocks: startup check accepts=True (num_blocks=70)
    step   3 scheduled=  240 computed= 1008 free=  1 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
    step   4 scheduled=   15 computed= 1023 free=  0 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
  VERDICT prompt=1023: finished=False computed=1023 preemptions=0 status=RUNNING
```

One block of headroom is the entire difference. Note that the prefill dies at exactly
1008 tokens, which is `(69 - 1 - 5) * 16` — the sequence length the pool can actually
serve.

### The fix

One function computes the bound, and it is the function the startup error message
already uses:

- `max_servable_num_tokens(vllm_config, kv_cache_groups, num_blocks)` in
  `kv_cache_utils.py` — the longest sequence a pool of `num_blocks` blocks can hold
  for one request. It is `_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups` (the helper behind
  "the estimated maximum model length" that `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` prints)
  evaluated against `num_blocks - 1` blocks, i.e. against the capacity `BlockPool`
  will actually hand out. It returns `None` for group layouts that cannot be priced
  per block — exactly the layouts whose pool was not sized per block either — so it
  never invents a bound the startup check did not apply.
- `Scheduler` evaluates it once at construction. When it is below `max_model_len` the
  configuration cannot serve its own window, which is logged at `ERROR` with the
  number the operator needs. A request past the bound can never be scheduled at any
  future time, however much drains, so `add_request` fails it immediately instead of
  queueing it: no prefill is spent, nothing is preempted, and the client gets a
  terminal response rather than a request that never returns.

So there is one bound with two call sites, which is the point:
`_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups` is called by the startup check
(`kv_cache_utils.py:2234`, via `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory`) and now by
`max_servable_num_tokens`, which is what the scheduler admits against. Neither side
can grow its own formula without the other seeing it.

The failure uses `RequestStatus.FINISHED_IGNORED`, which `vllm/v1/request.py` already
documents as the status for "requests whose prompt lengths are longer than the
model's length cap", mapping to `finish_reason="length"`. `FinishReason.ERROR` is
documented as a *retryable* internal error always converted to a 500, which is the
wrong contract here. Returning a literal 400 would mean exposing the pool-derived
bound to `input_processor._validate_prompt_len`, where `max_model_len` is validated;
happy to do that in a follow-up if maintainers prefer it — it is a frontend/engine-core
plumbing change and I kept it out of this PR.

Behaviour is unchanged whenever the pool covers `max_model_len`, which is every
correctly-sized deployment: the bound is then `>= max_model_len`, `_is_unservable`
short-circuits on the first comparison, and nothing is rejected. The 70-block row
above is byte-for-byte identical before and after.

### Relationship to #47272 — scoped around it, not a duplicate

I read #47272 ("Reserve the KV null block when validating `max_model_len`") before
writing any code, and this PR is deliberately scoped around it.

- **#47272 owns the capacity side.** It subtracts one block from the memory the
  startup check validates against, so a pool that cannot serve `max_model_len` is
  refused at boot with the existing message naming the estimated maximum model
  length. That is the right place for it and this PR does not touch that code path.
  Applied to the reproduction above, #47272 makes the 69-block pool illegal at
  startup — which is a better outcome than anything the scheduler can do, and is why
  I am not proposing an alternative to it.
- **This PR owns the request side.** It makes the runtime bound the same function as
  the startup bound, and gives the engine an answer for a request it cannot serve
  other than retrying it. That is needed independently of #47272, because the
  scheduler currently has *no* concept of "this request can never be scheduled": it
  only distinguishes "not now". If #47272 lands, this PR's check becomes dormant on
  correctly-sized pools (bound `>= max_model_len`) and remains the backstop for the
  paths #47272 does not cover — notably `_auto_fit_max_model_len`, which runs before
  #47272's reservation and can still land on the boundary.
- The two compose cleanly and neither subsumes the other. **Please do not merge this
  instead of #47272.**

Other prior art I checked: **#40946** (merged) is the design precedent — it fixed the
same class of defect (startup pool sizing and runtime admission using different
formulas) for SWA/chunked-local by putting the bound in one method called from both
sites, and this PR follows that shape. **#35541** (closed not-planned/stale) asked for
"abort requests that can never fit in the KV cache block pool with a clear error
rather than hanging indefinitely" — this is that, for the mechanism above. **#40384**
is why the numbers here are stated in blocks and tokens rather than inverted from the
`GPU KV cache size` log line, which on a hybrid model is
`num_blocks // len(kv_cache_groups) * min_block_size`.

### Scope of the claim

The field trace in #52520 came from a **downstream fork build** on a hybrid Qwen3.5
model (261,794-token request, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, MTP
depth 3, pool within ~1 % of the window; 63 full re-prefills over 656 s with zero
output tokens). The mechanism above is upstream code, and everything in this PR is
demonstrated on **stock `main` at `4d2a68d64d9e05921ed5c4099146e768a92d71d5`** by the
CPU-only unit test below — no GPU, no model weights, no fork code involved.

One part of the original report I could **not** reproduce on `main` and am therefore
not claiming: `vllm:num_preemptions_total` staying at `0.0` across the re-prefills.
On `main` the self-preemption path does increment `request.num_preemptions` and record
`EngineCoreEventType.PREEMPTED`, which `IterationStats` counts into
`vllm:num_preemptions_total`. So there is no accounting fix here, and I am not filing
one. (With this PR the point is moot for this defect: nothing is preempted, because
nothing is admitted, and the operator gets two `ERROR` lines naming the limit.)

### The decode case, added in the second commit

Review raised it and I measured it on the same stock-`main` harness: the admission
gate bounds a request on `num_tokens + 1`, but a generate request grows to
`prompt + max_tokens`. With `block_size` 16, `max_model_len` 1024 and the 69-block
pool above (`max_servable_num_tokens` 1008), `prompt=1000, max_tokens=24` clears the
frontend (`1000 + 24 <= 1024`, `vllm/renderers/params.py:210,442`) and clears
admission (`1000 + 1 <= 1008`), and then reaches 1009 tokens at output token 9. On
`main` it is preempted there, is now too long to re-prefill, and the next **3987
scheduler steps schedule zero tokens, produce no output and leave all 68 blocks
free** — the same terminal state as the prefill case, reached through decode.

Bounding admission on `num_tokens + max_tokens` would close it, but would refuse
requests that stop well before the wall: on that same pool, `max_tokens=8` runs to
completion in 12 steps. So the ceiling is applied where it belongs, as a length cap:
`check_stop` takes `max_servable_num_tokens` instead of `max_model_len`. Those are
equal on every pool that covers its window — `_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups`
searches with `right = original_max` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:1960`), and the
scheduler falls back to `max_model_len` when there is no per-block bound — so the
common path is unchanged. Where they differ the request stops on the ceiling and
returns its tokens with `finish_reason: length`, exactly as if `max_model_len` had
been set to what the pool can serve.

That is one bound with three call sites: startup sizing, admission, and the length
cap.

The spec-decode lookahead can also reach past the ceiling, because the running path
asks for `1 + len(spec_token_ids)` slots. Measured on stock `main` with drafts
injected: it preempts twice and then finishes, because preemption clears
`spec_token_ids` and the retry decodes into the cap. Bounded and self-correcting, so
`sched/scheduler.py:605` is left alone.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py
# surrounding suite, unchanged behaviour:
pytest tests/v1/core/
```

`tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py` is CPU-only
(`pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test`), built the same way as
`tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py`: a real `Scheduler` over a hand-built
hybrid `KVCacheConfig`, driven with `schedule()` / `update_from_output()`. No model
weights, no GPU. Seven cases:

1. `test_max_servable_num_tokens_reserves_the_null_block` — the bound is
   `(69 - 1 - 5) * 16 = 1008` at the startup minimum, and `>= max_model_len` with one
   block of headroom.
2. `test_unservable_request_is_failed_not_prefilled_and_retried` — the regression
   test. A 1023-token request on the 69-block pool: nothing is scheduled, it is
   finished as `FINISHED_IGNORED`, `num_computed_tokens == 0`,
   `num_preemptions == 0`, and no unfinished request is left behind.
3. `test_request_at_the_bound_is_failed_because_it_needs_an_output_slot` — the bound
   is a sequence length, so a prompt of exactly 1008 is already too long (it was the
   one length that prefilled fully on `main` and then stalled on its first decode
   step).
4. `test_servable_request_at_the_same_pool_still_runs` — 1007 tokens on the *same*
   69-block pool prefills fully, decodes, and finishes. The bound must not
   over-reject.
5. `test_pool_with_headroom_serves_the_whole_window` — 1023 tokens on a 70-block pool
   behaves exactly as before this PR.
6. `test_generation_stops_at_the_bound_instead_of_stalling_mid_decode` — the decode
   regression test. `prompt=1000, max_tokens=24` on the 69-block pool clears both
   length checks, then must finish `FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED` at 1008 tokens with
   `num_preemptions == 0` and nothing left unfinished.
7. `test_generation_is_not_capped_when_the_pool_covers_the_window` — the same request
   with one block of headroom must still produce all 24 tokens, so the length cap
   cannot silently truncate generation on the common path.

## Test Result

The new file, checked out on top of unmodified `main` at `4d2a68d6` (the fix reverted,
the test kept), fails:

```text
$ git checkout HEAD -- vllm/ && pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py -q
FAILED test_max_servable_num_tokens_reserves_the_null_block
  - AttributeError: 'Scheduler' object has no attribute 'max_servable_num_tokens'
FAILED test_unservable_request_is_failed_not_prefilled_and_retried
  - AssertionError: assert not {'0': 256}
FAILED test_request_at_the_bound_is_failed_because_it_needs_an_output_slot
  - AssertionError: assert not {'0': 256}
FAILED test_generation_stops_at_the_bound_instead_of_stalling_mid_decode
  - AttributeError: 'Scheduler' object has no attribute 'max_servable_num_tokens'
FAILED test_generation_is_not_capped_when_the_pool_covers_the_window
  - AttributeError: 'Scheduler' object has no attribute 'max_servable_num_tokens'
5 failed, 2 passed, 14 warnings in 4.81s
```

`{'0': 256}` is `main` admitting the unservable request and scheduling the first
256-token prefill chunk of the sequence it will then throw away. The two that pass
before and after are the two "must still work" directions — they are there to catch
over-rejection and over-capping, and they must never have gone red.

Reverting only the one-line length cap and keeping everything else isolates the
decode case:

```text
$ sed -i 's/self.max_servable_num_tokens)/self.max_model_len)/' <the check_stop call>
$ pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py -q
FAILED test_generation_stops_at_the_bound_instead_of_stalling_mid_decode
  - assert <RequestStatus.PREEMPTED: 6> == <RequestStatus.FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED: 8>
1 failed, 6 passed, 14 warnings in 4.92s
```

With the fix:

```text
$ pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py -q
.......                                                                  [100%]
7 passed, 14 warnings in 4.71s
```

Surrounding suite, same command on `4d2a68d6` and on this branch:

```text
main @ 4d2a68d6 : 2 failed, 495 passed, 2 errors in 348.75s
this branch     : 2 failed, 502 passed, 2 errors in 375.92s
```

The same two failures and the same two setup errors occur on both, all environmental
in my CPU-only sandbox and unrelated to this change: failures in
`test_scheduler.py::test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`
and `test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py::test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e`, and setup errors on
`test_concurrent_partial_prefill` and `test_prefix_cache_stats_is_recorded` — all four
need a GPU-backed engine core. The +7 are the new tests.

Two existing tests build a `Scheduler` with `object.__new__` and set its attributes by
hand; they each gain one line for the new `unservable_reqs` set and one for
`max_servable_num_tokens`
(`tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`).

Lint gates on the changed files:

```text
$ ruff check <changed files>          # 0.14.0, as pinned in .pre-commit-config.yaml
All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check <changed files>
5 files already formatted

(clean)
$ python tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12 <changed files>   # mypy 1.20.2
Success: no issues found in 2 source files
Success: no issues found in 3 source files
```

---

AI assistance was used to investigate and draft this change; every changed line was
reviewed, and the reproduction, the tests and the lint gates were run locally as
described above.
