items.title: [Bug]: hybrid Mamba + `--mamba-cache-mode align`: a request near the KV-pool ceiling is admitted, prefilled to 98.9 %, requeued, and re-prefilled forever with zero output tokens and zero preemption accounting
items.body:
### Your current environment

This is a **downstream fork build**, and I want that on the record before the trace, because
it determines what I am and am not claiming (see *Scope of the claim* at the bottom).

```text
vllm 0.11.2.dev280+gilded.gnosis.v20.vllm4d006a4.b12xcd3ce19.fi1ac6942.cu132.20260810.r34
  (local-inference-lab/vllm @ dev/gilded-gnosis, upstream integration tree 4d006a43928cdee0…,
   base image built 2026-08-10)
container image  localhost/vllm:gg-r34-patched-apc
                 sha256:16a936b877b90fc080181e842f47dbafc5cb8e62688799596836e34ba0b79218
  (built FROM the published base docker.io/voipmonitor/vllm@sha256:820181fbbc975cd5291c411cda…,
   adding exactly one file: see next paragraph)
torch 2.12.0+cu132, FlashInfer @ 1ac6942, python 3.12.3
GPU        1x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, 32,607 MiB, SM 12.0, driver 610.57.04, CUDA UMD 13.3
host       Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.8.0-137-generic, podman 4.9.3 rootless
model      Qwen3.8-27B (Qwen3.5 architecture: hybrid GDN linear-attention + full attention),
           EXL3-quantised weights, --kv-cache-dtype fp8
```

**The scheduler in this image is upstream's own post-#51113 file.** `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`
is the vendored r34 copy with exactly the two behavioural hunks of
[#51113](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51113) (`c56f169d9ae4`) applied,
`sha256 b431c1066dfee3ed56bfa7e71cc8606f9afadc300f22d7fc542c43835d1b22bf`; upstream's own
`tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` from that merge commit passes 20/20 against it
and fails 14/20 against the unpatched copy. So this is **not** #43559 or #51113 resurfacing, and
it is not the encoder-cap zero-collapse livelock of #51603 / #40757 either — see *Prior art* below.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On a hybrid Mamba model with `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, a request whose
length sits close to the KV pool is **accepted** by admission, prefilled to ~99 % of the pool,
dropped back to the waiting queue with the pool freed to 0 %, and prefilled again — forever.

The cycle has a fixed 30-second period. Prompt throughput pins at ~960 tok/s, generation
throughput is `0.0` for the whole run, and **not one output token is ever produced**. The HTTP
request never returns and the server never recovers. It is not wedged — it is busy — so it
presents as a very slow request rather than as a hang, and a liveness probe on `/health` keeps
passing.

Two properties make this worse than a plain admission misjudgement:

1. **`vllm:num_preemptions_total` stays at `0.0`.** Nothing is preempted, because nothing is ever
   admitted to `running` for long enough to count. The only observable is
   `vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason{reason="capacity"} = 1`, which is indistinguishable from a
   healthy server that is momentarily full. There is no counter that says "this request was
   descheduled after partial prefill", so no alert can fire.
2. **The work is discarded, not published.** Over the run the engine logged **261,794 prefix-cache
   queries and exactly 0 hits**. The cache was consulted on every retry and had nothing to offer, so
   every retry costs full price and no retry can ever cost less. That is what converts a one-off
   admission error into an unbounded one.

   *I now believe property 2 is an instance of the already-reported #45238 rather than a new
   finding — see Prior art. I am keeping it in the trace because it is the reason the loop is
   stable, but I am not claiming it as new.*

### Observed cycle

```text
INFO 08-16 05:37:17 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 800.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 98.9%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%
INFO 08-16 05:37:27 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 959.9 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%
INFO 08-16 05:37:37 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 960.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%
INFO 08-16 05:37:47 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 799.9 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 98.9%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%
INFO 08-16 05:37:57 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 960.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%
INFO 08-16 05:38:07 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 960.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 0 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.0%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%
INFO 08-16 05:38:17 [loggers.py:314] Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 800.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 98.9%, Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%
```

63 such lines. Stopped by the operator after 656 s; nothing in the trace suggests it would ever
terminate. `/metrics` at the moment of teardown:

```text
vllm:num_requests_running                                   0.0
vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason{reason="capacity"}      1.0
vllm:num_preemptions_total                                  0.0
vllm:prefix_cache_queries_total                       261,794.0
vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total                                0.0
```

### Reproduction

One request, one server. `--max-num-seqs 1`, so there is no concurrency and no second request
involved in the failure.

Exact server argv as run (EXL3 quantisation flags are ours; the scheduler-relevant flags are the
last eight):

```sh
podman run --rm --device nvidia.com/gpu=all --ipc=host --network host \
  -e PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
  --entrypoint /opt/venv/bin/vllm localhost/vllm:gg-r34-patched-apc \
  serve /models/ctx-repo/snapshots/c45c273b0d6ef2859cb2d85b36dd52253c80d878 \
  --served-model-name m \
  --quantization exl3 \
  --quantization-config '{"linear":{"weight":"mxfp8"},"ignore":["re:.*visual\\..*","re:.*in_proj_a$","re:.*in_proj_b$","re:.*in_proj_ba$","re:.*mtp\\..*","lm_head"]}' \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9585 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --mm-processor-kwargs '{"truncation":false,"max_pixels":8388608}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[4]}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8251
```

Startup banner confirms the flags took effect, so this is not a silently-ignored flag:

```text
'enable_prefix_caching': True
'mamba_cache_mode': 'align'
Prefix caching in Mamba cache 'align' mode is currently enabled
Setting attention block size to 1600 tokens
Add 3 padding layers, may waste at most 6.25% KV cache memory
Available KV cache memory: 9.39 GiB
GPU KV cache size: 265,072 tokens
Maximum concurrency for 262,144 tokens per request: 1.01x
```

Then one request: a 261,794-token text prompt (a "needle" document with a 10-digit code at depth
0.5), `max_tokens=16`, `temperature=0`. It never returns.

The **shape** that matters, for anyone reproducing on stock vLLM with a Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5-family
checkpoint and no EXL3 involved:

- hybrid Mamba/GDN model, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`
- speculative decoding on (`mtp`, or anything that makes `use_eagle()` true), `num_speculative_tokens ≥ 1`
- `--gpu-memory-utilization` tuned so `GPU KV cache size` is a **few thousand tokens above**
  `--max-model-len` (here: pool 265,072 vs window 262,144, engine's own "Maximum concurrency" 1.01x)
- one request whose prompt is within ~1 % of `--max-model-len`
- `--max-num-seqs 1`, `--max-num-batched-tokens` well below the mamba block size, so the prefill is
  chunked and the failure lands on the final allocation rather than the first

### Why the startup check does not catch it, and the arithmetic

`Setting attention block size to 1600 tokens` — the mamba page size forces the attention block size
up from the default. With `align`, a request occupies **whole blocks**:

| term | value |
|---|---|
| prompt | 261,794 tokens |
| rounded to whole 1,600-token blocks | `cdiv(261794, 1600) = 164` blocks = 262,400 slots |
| plus MTP-3 lookahead slots | `num_lookahead_tokens = 3` (`scheduler.py:238-262`) |
| plus the mamba group's own running-state and speculative blocks | `1 + num_speculative_blocks` blocks, from the same pool (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1532-1534`) |
| plus `BlockPool`'s permanently reserved null block | 1 block (this is #47272's point) |
| pool reported by the engine | 265,072 tokens |

The pool *looks* like it has 3,278 tokens of slack over the rounded prompt, and the startup check
passes. (Deliberately stated in tokens: `GPU KV cache size` on a hybrid model cannot be inverted into
a block count — see the note below — so I am not claiming that slack is worth any particular number
of blocks.) It is not enough once every term above is added, and the engine only discovers this at
the **final** allocation of the prefill — after ~260 k tokens of work have already been done and
thrown away.

The asymmetry between the two formulas is visible in the source. The startup sizer's per-request
bound for the attention group is:

```python
# vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:291-298  AttentionSpec.max_memory_usage_bytes
return cdiv(max_model_len, self.block_size) * self.page_size_bytes
```

`cdiv(max_model_len, block_size)` pages and nothing else: no lookahead slots, no decode block, no
null block. Runtime admission for the same request goes through:

```python
# vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:958-959  (waiting queue)
new_blocks = self.kv_cache_manager.allocate_slots(
    ..., num_lookahead_tokens=effective_lookahead_tokens, ...)

# vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:430-431
num_tokens_need_slot = min(num_tokens_main_model + num_lookahead_tokens, self.max_model_len)
```

and, for the mamba group in align mode, through:

```python
# vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1507-1509
num_required_blocks = cdiv(num_tokens, self.block_size) + self.num_speculative_blocks
# :1532-1534, first prefill
num_new_blocks = 1 + self.num_speculative_blocks + int(has_partial_hit)
```

**What I have proven and what I have not.** The behaviour above is measured. The exact term that
tips the final allocation over is *not* proven by me: `GPU KV cache size` on a hybrid model is a
derived figure (`num_blocks // len(kv_cache_groups) * min_block_size`, the subject of #40384), so I
cannot recover the block-level counts from the log line, and the card this ran on is not available
for an instrumented rerun. What I can say is that the startup bound omits at least the null block
(#47272) and the lookahead slots, that admission demands both, and that at 1,600-token blocks each
omitted page is 0.61 % of a 262 k window — which is precisely the size of the gap. **If a maintainer
tells me which counters to dump, I will run an instrumented reproduction and post the block-level
numbers.**

### Measured band, one engine start per row, identical flags otherwise

| `--gpu-memory-utilization` | available KV | `GPU KV cache size` | max concurrency @262,144 | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.955  | 9.28 GiB | — | — | **refuses to start**: needs 9.29 GiB, suggests max len 260,800 |
| 0.9555 | 9.30 GiB | 262,144 | 1.00x | starts, then **deadlocks** mid-prefill, `reason="capacity"`, 0 tok/s |
| 0.958  | 9.38 GiB | 263,608 | 1.01x | starts (no request sent) |
| 0.9585 | 9.39 GiB | 265,072 | 1.01x | starts, then **livelocks**: 30 s re-prefill cycle, 0 output tokens |
| 0.959  | 9.41 GiB | 265,072 | 1.01x | starts (identical pool) |
| 0.96   | 9.44 GiB | 265,072 | 1.01x | starts (identical pool) |

Two things fall out of the band:

- The pool is quantised: 0.9585, 0.959 and 0.96 all yield the same 265,072 tokens. So on this card
  **there is no `--gpu-memory-utilization` that makes a 262,144-token request schedulable under
  align mode.** The configuration is unserviceable, and every value of the knob either refuses to
  start or livelocks.
- The 0.9555 row (pool exactly `max_model_len`, "Maximum concurrency … 1.00x", then 0 tok/s) is,
  as far as I can tell, exactly the boundary case #47272 describes and fixes.

The same build with `--max-model-len 256000` at 0.9585 (pool 264,777, 1.03x) serves a 254,964-token
needle exactly in 179 s, then serves a second 254,967-token needle in the same process after the
first is released. So the feature itself works; it is specifically the
request-close-to-the-pool case that fails.

### Expected behaviour

In rough order of value:

1. **Reject at admission.** A request whose rounded, lookahead-inclusive, null-block-inclusive
   requirement exceeds the *whole pool* can never be scheduled at any future time, no matter what
   else drains. It should fail with a 400-class error naming the maximum servable length — the same
   information `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` already prints at startup — rather than being
   accepted and retried forever. #35541 asked for exactly this and was closed as stale.
2. **Make the startup bound and the admission bound the same function**, the way #40946 did for
   SWA/chunked-local by introducing `max_admission_blocks_per_request` on the spec and calling it
   from both `max_memory_usage_bytes` and `get_num_blocks_to_allocate`. The align-mode rounding, the
   lookahead slots and the null block belong in that one function, so the two paths cannot drift.
   Today a configuration that cannot serve one native-length request still boots.
3. **Account for it.** A request descheduled after partial prefill should increment a preemption or
   restart counter. `num_preemptions_total = 0.0` through 63 full re-prefills of a 261 k prompt is a
   monitoring blind spot independent of the allocation bug: the only signal is a `waiting` gauge
   that healthy back-pressure produces too.
4. Optionally, bound the retries: a request that has been descheduled from the same admission
   decision N times without gaining ground should be failed rather than retried.

### Prior art I checked, and how this differs

Searched `vllm-project/vllm`, issues and PRs, open and closed (queries recorded in our receipt,
linked below).

- **#47272** *(open PR, "Reserve the KV null block when validating max_model_len")* — **the closest
  thing to a duplicate, for one of my six rows.** Its exact-boundary case ("passes the check,
  logs `Maximum concurrency … 1.00x`, is one usable block short at runtime, engine hangs at 0
  tok/s") is my 0.9555 row. It does not cover align-mode whole-block rounding or the lookahead
  slots, and it does not address the retry loop or the missing accounting.
  I have posted the six-row band as a comment there: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47272#issuecomment-5307330064 .
- **#35541** *(closed as not-planned/stale)* — asked for exactly recommendation 1 ("vLLM should
  abort requests that can never fit in the KV cache block pool with a clear error, rather than
  hanging indefinitely"). Different mechanism: there the request never starts (`allocate_slots`
  returns `None` immediately). Here it prefills to 98.9 % first, which is what burns the GPU.
- **#45238** *(open)* — align mode registers only ~1–2 mamba block hashes per request, and
  `HybridKVCacheCoordinator` requires every group to hit, so a mamba miss vetoes the attention
  matches and the hit rate collapses to 0 %. I believe this **is** the explanation of my 261,794
  queries / 0 hits, so I am *not* offering that as a new finding.
- **#51603** *(merged)* and **#51582** / **#40757** / **#40707** — mamba-align livelocks where
  `_mamba_block_aligned_split` collapses a chunk to **zero** tokens because a multimodal encoder cap
  landed mid-block, so the request makes no progress at all. Different trigger (encoder cache, not
  the KV pool), different signature (0 tokens scheduled vs a full 260 k prefill each cycle), and
  text-only here — no multimodal item is in this request. #51603 is merged and is *not* in this
  build; it would not change this trace.
- **#40946** *(merged)* — same *class* of defect (runtime admission and startup pool sizing using
  different formulas) for SWA/chunked-local, and the design I am pointing at in recommendation 2.
- **#45387 / #45388** *(closed)* — permanent scheduler deadlock under KV-cache pressure, but the
  root cause is an unconditional `break` blocking `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` promotion with a KV
  offloading connector enabled. No connector is enabled here.
- **#38516** *(closed as stale)*, **#50509** *(open)* — both about the startup check being
  unfriendly/overridable. Neither is about admission accepting what it cannot schedule.
- Nothing found for: an accepted request being re-prefilled on a fixed period with zero output;
  `num_preemptions_total` staying at 0 across repeated partial prefills; or align-mode rounding
  being absent from the startup bound.

### Scope of the claim

I can support this **on the fork build named above**, and I say plainly that I have **not**
reproduced it on stock vLLM and do not claim it there. What I can say about the transfer: the
scheduler file involved is upstream's own post-#51113 copy, the flags are upstream's, the
`kv_cache_interface.py` / `kv_cache_manager.py` / `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` lines quoted
above are unmodified vendored upstream code in this image, and nothing in the mechanism touches
EXL3 weights, this fork's kernels, or the quantisation path — the failure is a block-count decision
taken before any kernel runs. So I would expect any hybrid-Mamba deployment running align mode with
speculative decoding and a request near its pool ceiling to hit it, but that is an expectation, not
a measurement. The card is a single physical RTX 5090 shared with other work; if a maintainer wants
a stock-vLLM reproduction (BF16 Qwen3-Next at a window sized to its own pool), say so and I will
schedule one.

### Evidence

Full artefacts — the 63-line timeline, every per-probe engine banner, every launch argv, the seven
server logs with their sha256s, and the `/metrics` scrape:
`receipts/qualification-5090-apc.json` and `receipts/qual-apc-raw/` in
<https://github.com/malaiwah/qwen38-27b-exl3>. The prior-art search log, with every query, is in
`receipts/upstream-issue-sweep.json` in the same repository. The fork-side record of this trace is
local-inference-lab/vllm#394.

### Before submitting a new issue…

- [x] Searched for relevant issues (queries recorded and published; see *Prior art*).

items.title: [Performance] DP8 vs TP8 for single-KV-head MLA: 7.7x KV, 3.4x faster 1M TTFT at c=8 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, 8x B200, vLLM v0.25.0)
items.body:
### Summary

On a single 8x NVIDIA B200 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0` serves `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (304B total / 13B active, MLA, 1M context, FP4 experts + FP8 KV) with measured multi-session 1M-context concurrency that has not been published before for this model class.

The headline finding: **parallelism shape matters more than any tuning knob for this model.** The recipes-page default (TP8) reports a startup-log KV budget of 20.43x maximum concurrency for 1,048,576-token requests, i.e. KV capacity for ~20 simultaneous 1M-token sessions ("c" throughout this report = concurrent requests). Switching to `--data-parallel-size 8` reports **156.9x**, a 7.7x improvement, because MLA's single KV head cannot be sharded across tensor-parallel ranks, so TP8 replicates the KV cache 8x; under DP8 (with `--enable-expert-parallel`) each GPU holds an independent KV pool for the data-parallel attention path, while the MoE experts remain sharded EP8 across GPUs (not replicated). For scale: V4-Pro's startup log on the same host class reported 2.0x for the same 1M request shape (vllm-project/vllm#43753; same startup-log KV-budget figure, different model). Both DP8 figures are KV-budget capacity, validated empirically to c=16 in this report, not to c=156.

Measured envelopes (cache-busted real-prose token IDs from the public-domain Federalist Papers corpus, 3 reps per cell, `max_tokens=64`, streaming, 600s client timeout on all cells):

| Parallelism | 1M c=8 TTFT p50 | 1M c=8 ok rate | 1M c=16 ok rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP8 (recipes default) | 314.6s | 24/24 (100%) | 27/48 (56%) |
| **DP8 (recommended)** | **84.7s** | **24/24 (100%)** | **48/48 (100%)** |

(Same-node controlled follow-up, posted as a comment on this issue: TTFT p50 ratio 3.44x; a fair statement of the DP8 advantage at 1M c=8 is 3.2-3.7x depending on metric and run.)

Additional findings:
- **DSpark speculative decoding at 1M context delivers 4.1x decode-window speedup (matched 0.85/0.85 util), and it exposes a metrics problem**: at 1M c=1 with `max_tokens=512`, DSpark decode-window TPOT is 2.08ms vs vanilla 8.44ms (both at 0.85 util, real Federalist prose, 3 reps; decode-window TPOT = `(wall - TTFT) / (completion_tokens - 1)`). But streaming inter-arrival TPOT reports 11.18ms, 5.4x higher than the decode-window TPOT, because 512 tokens arrive in ~96 stream chunks under 5-token speculation, and the inter-arrival mean divides by chunks not tokens. Vanilla streaming TPOT (8.97ms) closely matches its decode-window TPOT (8.44ms) because tokens arrive individually (details in the DSpark section). Crossover: tail-latency collapse at c>=4 on the tested 8K TP8 cells (mean TPOT explodes while p50 stays single-digit).
- **Prefix-cache warm-document: 22x speedup**: first question on a 1M-token document in 66s, every follow-up in ~3s.
- torch.compile is not supported for this model on v0.25.0; the auto-disable via `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` appears intentional (vLLM warns the model does not support it; confirmation requested in ask 2).
- Increasing `--max-num-batched-tokens` beyond 8192 yields no TTFT improvement and costs 32% of KV capacity.

Context for why this model matters: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 is currently the #3 open-weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (retrieved 2026-08-07) at very low per-task cost; this report adds a measured 1M-context concurrency envelope for it on a single node.

Prior art: vllm-project/vllm#43753 (DeepSeek-V4-Pro 1M on 8x B200, same host class). V4-Pro's startup log reported 2.0x max concurrency at 1M and our testing there topped out at "1M c=2, isolated queue." V4-Flash-0731 on DP8 serves 1M c=16 with 100% success.

**Updates** (body revised with follow-up work; the linked comments are the audit trail):

- 2026-08-07: DP8/EP8 mechanism wording corrected (attention/KV data-parallel; experts EP-sharded, not replicated); focused recipes proposal filed as vllm-project/recipes#762.
- 2026-08-08: same-node TP8-vs-DP8 bridge posted (closes the cross-node limitation); title and headline restated to the controlled 3.4x figure, range 3.2-3.7x.
- 2026-08-08: measured DP8 mitigation for ask 4 (single-1M mixed workload, same node: short TTFT p50 63.9s to 0.57s, ~112x, 1M unchanged); ask 4 narrowed to TP8 deployments and the all-replicas-busy case ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51454#issuecomment-5229675310)).

### Maintainer asks

1. **DP8 vs TP8 for MLA models**: The recipes-page B200 profile uses `--tensor-parallel-size 8`, but `--data-parallel-size 8` delivers 7.7x more total KV capacity and 3.4x faster TTFT at 1M c=8 for this model (same-node controlled measurement; 3.7x in the original cross-node ladder, see the follow-up comment). Should the recipes page recommend DP8 as the default for concurrency- and long-context-oriented serving of single-KV-head MLA models, keeping TP8 for latency-critical single-stream (c=1-2; our measured break-even is c=3)? Is this a known property that could be surfaced more prominently?

2. **torch.compile auto-disable**: `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1` is auto-set for this model, disabling torch.compile (`mode=NONE`). Forcing `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` turns on `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`, but vLLM warns "the model does not support it." Is this intentional, and is torch.compile support planned for DeepSeek-V4-Flash on a future tag?

3. **Speculative-decode metrics on stable**: streaming inter-arrival TPOT is not interpretable under speculative burst delivery: our matched-util A/B shows it reporting 11.18ms (5.4x higher than the true decode-window TPOT of 2.08ms) because 512 tokens arrive in ~96 stream chunks under 5-token speculation, and the inter-arrival mean divides by chunks not tokens. Decode-window TPOT `(wall - TTFT) / (completion_tokens - 1)` is the correct metric but requires `max_tokens` large enough for a measurable decode window. Acceptance-rate fields (`verifier_accept_len`) are nightly-only, so on v0.25.0 stable there is no built-in way to quantify spec-decode speedup from the serving API. Ask: would you accept exposing acceptance-length and decode-window metrics on stable, or documenting that TPOT metrics are burst-artifacted under spec decode? We are happy to file this as a separate metrics issue if preferred.

4. **Mixed-workload scheduler knobs**: `--long-prefill-token-threshold` and `--scheduling-policy priority` (with per-request priorities) have no effect on short-request TTFT beside a 1M prefill on v0.25.0. `--max-num-partial-prefills > 1` raises `NotImplementedError`. Is improved prefill preemption planned for a future release? This is the most operationally important gap: serving 1M-context requests alongside short requests without queue isolation currently starves the short requests for the full prefill duration (~65s). Follow-up (2026-08-08): monolithic DP8 avoids this for the single-long-prefill case via replica isolation (~112x short-TTFT improvement at p50, same-node A/B; [details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51454#issuecomment-5229675310)), so this ask now primarily concerns TP8 deployments and the case where long prefills occupy all DP replicas.

5. **DSpark stable-vs-nightly knob gap**: `verifier_accept_len` and `dspark_block_size` are nightly-only speculative-config fields (pydantic rejects them on v0.25.0). The recipes-page B200 cell pins a nightly tag. Is there a timeline for these knobs to reach stable?

6. **`draft_sample_method` discrepancy**: The HF model card says `greedy`; the vLLM recipes page emits `probabilistic`. We A/B tested both on real prose (7 cells, 3 reps each): no significant difference (greedy 0-16% slower at c=1, identical at c=2+). Ask: align the recipes page with the HF card (or document why `probabilistic` is emitted); this is a one-line recipes-repo fix and we can file it there if preferred.

Note on routing: asks 1 and 6 may belong on the recipes repo and ask 3 could be a standalone metrics issue; we kept them here for context and will split on maintainer preference.

### Environment

| Component | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Cloud / instance | Nebius AI Cloud, two preemptible 8-GPU nodes. Node 1: correctness suite, real-prose ladder, TP8 concurrency envelope, tuning sweeps, first DSpark probe. Node 2: DP8 1M ladder, KV-eviction probe, scheduler-knob experiment, DSpark crossover. Same image + model snapshot on both; KV capacity verified identical. |
| GPUs | 8x NVIDIA B200 SXM6 |
| GPU architecture | SM100 |
| VRAM | 183,359 MiB per GPU |
| Driver | 580.126.09 (node 1) / 580.173.02 (node 2) |
| Model | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, snapshot `7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062` |
| Model on disk | 155.4 GiB, 48 safetensors shards |
| Serving image | `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0`. Hub amd64 digest `sha256:e1c1ff1af9a15921bfa11d1d95047258c1797392cdbfa296e7639da446b23f97`; pull manifest digest `sha256:fc56161ee42a`; local image ID `sha256:d5219758abb3` (same image, three identifier forms) |
| vLLM version | 0.25.0 (V1 engine), build commit `dd10e03f95f94edbea1975c67ace3a35ec9a8a40` |
| Python | 3.12 |
| CUDA / PyTorch | CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 |
| NCCL | 2.28.9 |
| Triton | 3.6.0 |
| FlashInfer | 0.6.13 |
| DeepEP | 1.2.1+73b6ea4 |
| Transformers | 5.13.0 |
| Accelerate | 1.14.0 |
| huggingface_hub | 1.23.0 |

Provenance: all version rows captured from in-container `pip freeze`, `torch.cuda.nccl.version()`, `nvidia-smi`, and vLLM startup logs. Full 262-package pip freeze available with proof artifacts on request.

### Launch command (TP8, recipes-page default)

```bash
docker run -d --name v4flash0731 --gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size 32g \
  --ulimit nofile=1048576:1048576 \
  -v /data/hf-cache:/root/.cache/huggingface -p 8000:8000 \
  vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0 \
  /root/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/snapshots/7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4-flash-0731 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention_config.use_fp4_indexer_cache=True \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95
```

Startup log: KV cache 21,419,891 tokens, 20.43x max concurrency at 1M per request. Engine init ~367s.

### Launch command (DP8, recommended for concurrency)

Same as above but replace `--tensor-parallel-size 8` with `--data-parallel-size 8`.

Startup log: KV cache 20,571,235 tokens per replica × 8 = 164.6M total, 156.9x max concurrency at 1M (theoretical capacity from KV budget; tested empirically to c=16, not c=156). `compilation_config.mode=NONE` (same as TP8 with breakable CUDA graphs).

### Launch command (DSpark, for interactive c=1-3)

Same as TP8 but `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` (draft head requires ~6 GiB/GPU) and add:

```bash
--speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/root/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/snapshots/7872f01b1d1fe23eabc4c98b48bffcef5a386062","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

Startup log: KV cache 17,954,198 tokens / 17.12x at 1M (reduced from 21.4M due to lower util + draft head). DSpark draft model: 96M params. Note: `--max-num-partial-prefills > 1` raises `NotImplementedError` on v0.25.0. DSpark + DP8 failed to launch in our single attempt; we did not isolate whether the cause is memory or a config limitation, so we make no compatibility claim.

### Correctness / request-shape caveats

- v1.5 seven-prompt correctness suite under Think High (`reasoning_effort=high`, `max_tokens>=4096`): 7/7 PASS.
- Think Max: 6/7 pass; prompt 6 soft-fails (reasoning exhausted 4096 tokens; HF card recommends up to 384K output tokens for max mode).
- All performance cells use `temperature=0`, non-thinking completions (greedy decode). Thinking mode is not exercised in the concurrency envelope.
- All long-context cells use real-prose Federalist Papers token IDs, not synthetic random IDs. Cache-busting: per-repeat unique segment markers interspersed throughout the corpus (not just at the prefix), because vLLM's block-level prefix cache matches from any point where token sequences align.
- `n` disclosure: 3 reps per cell for both TP8 and DP8 envelopes. Requests within a rep start synchronized and share the batch, so the unit of experimental replication is the 3 batch reps, not the pooled request count; "24/24 ok" is a success count, not 24 independent samples. DP8 128K-512K measured on node 1 (driver 580.126.09); DP8 1M measured on node 2 (driver 580.173.02). Same Docker image (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.0`, manifest digest `sha256:fc56161ee42a`, local image ID `sha256:d5219758abb3`) and model snapshot on both nodes. KV capacity verified identical on both nodes (20,571,235 tokens/replica under DP8, 21,419,891 under TP8).

### Long-context real-prose envelope (c=1, TP8)

Federalist cache-busted ladder, 30/30 clean, steady-state TTFT medians:

| Context | TTFT p50 |
| --- | --- |
| 128K | 3.9s |
| 256K | 8.8s |
| 512K | 22.7s |
| 768K | 40.3s |
| 1M | 65.2s |

V4-Pro on the same host class: ~148s at 1M (from vllm-project/vllm#43753). V4-Flash-0731 is ~2.3x faster at 1M and ~3.3x faster at 128K.

### Concurrency envelope

#### TP8 (recipes-page default)

14 cells, 3 reps each, cache-busted Federalist prose, `max_tokens=64`, streaming:

| Context | c | ok | TTFT p50 | TTFT p99 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 128K | 8 | 24/24 | 18.5s | 29.3s |
| 128K | 16 | 48/48 | 33.0s | 69.8s |
| 128K | 32 | 96/96 | 61.8s | 116.1s |
| 128K | 64 | 192/192 | 119.8s | 231.8s |
| 256K | 8 | 24/24 | 41.9s | 80.9s |
| 256K | 16 | 48/48 | 75.2s | 133.0s |
| 256K | 32 | 96/96 | 141.3s | 265.4s |
| 512K | 4 | 12/12 | 65.6s | 87.1s |
| 512K | 8 | 24/24 | 108.4s | 172.8s |
| 512K | 16 | 48/48 | 172.5s | 345.2s |
| 1M | 2 | 6/6 | 65.4s | 127.7s |
| 1M | 4 | 12/12 | 190.0s | 252.4s |
| 1M | 8 | 24/24 | 314.6s | 501.5s |
| 1M | 16 | 27/48 | 314.5s | 563.8s |

Admission boundary at 1M c=16: 9/16 per rep succeed (56%); the 7 failures are client read-timeout at 600s. Successful requests at c=16 have the same TTFT p50 as c=8 (314.5s), suggesting the GPU is not overloaded but the prefill queue is too deep for the timeout. Caveat: because 44% of requests are censored at 600s, the c=16 success-only statistics carry survivorship bias (the true distribution's upper tail is cut off at the timeout); read this row as an admission-boundary marker, not a latency measurement.

Percentile note for both envelope tables: read p99 on 24-48-sample cells as the worst observed value, not a stable percentile; only the c=32/c=64 cells (96-192 samples) support percentile reads, and even there the batch reps (3) are the stronger unit of uncertainty.

#### DP8 (recommended)

All cells 3 reps, cache-busted Federalist prose. 128K-512K measured on node 1 (driver 580.126.09); 1M measured on node 2 (driver 580.173.02). Same image, same snapshot, same KV capacity (verified: 20,571,235 tokens/replica on both). Known limitation: the headline TP8-vs-DP8 1M comparison therefore crosses nodes. The same-node bridge run closed this (posted 2026-08-08 as a follow-up comment): TP8 and DP8 back to back on one host at 1M c=8 give DP8 3.44x on TTFT p50 and 3.2x on makespan and aggregate input throughput; a fair range across metrics and runs is 3.2-3.7x.

| Context | c | ok | TTFT p50 | TTFT p99 | vs TP8 speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 128K | 8 | 24/24 | 6.2s | 27.1s | 3.0x |
| 128K | 16 | 48/48 | 10.4s | 37.6s | 3.2x |
| 128K | 32 | 96/96 | 16.6s | 38.6s | 3.7x |
| 128K | 64 | 192/192 | 22.0s | 44.5s | 5.4x |
| 256K | 8 | 24/24 | 13.2s | 22.5s | 3.2x |
| 256K | 16 | 48/48 | 20.6s | 42.2s | 3.7x |
| 256K | 32 | 96/96 | 30.2s | 53.7s | 4.7x |
| 512K | 4 | 12/12 | 27.6s | 47.5s | 2.4x |
| 512K | 8 | 24/24 | 29.8s | 72.2s | 3.6x |
| 512K | 16 | 48/48 | 32.6s | 121.5s | 5.3x |
| 1M | 1 | 3/3 | 64.9s | 65.1s | 1.0x |
| 1M | 2 | 6/6 | 71.3s | 127.7s | 0.9x |
| 1M | 4 | 12/12 | 76.2s | 135.2s | 2.5x |
| 1M | 8 | 24/24 | 84.7s | 216.2s | 3.7x |
| 1M | 16 | 48/48 | 152.1s | 346.1s | 2.1x + 100% ok |

The speedup factor grows with both context length and concurrency, because DP8 distributes prefill across 8 independent GPU replicas rather than sharing one request across all 8 GPUs. The trade-off: 1M c=1-2 is comparable or slightly slower under DP8 (single-GPU prefill vs 8-GPU TP prefill). Break-even at c=3.

Root cause of the KV capacity delta: MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) uses 1 KV head. Under TP8, the KV cache cannot be sharded across tensor-parallel ranks and is replicated 8x. Under DP8 with `--enable-expert-parallel`, the attention/KV path is data-parallel: each GPU holds its own independent KV pool and runs the full attention stack, while the MoE expert weights remain sharded EP8 across all GPUs (not replicated); expert traffic crosses GPUs via EP all-to-all. So "independent" applies to the attention/KV state, not the whole model. The per-GPU KV pool is 20.6M tokens (vs TP8's 21.4M, slightly less due to per-GPU overhead), and 8 independent pools sum to 164.6M.

#### Aggregate input throughput (uncached prefill)

Computed from per-request `usage.prompt_tokens` and per-rep batch makespan, mean of 3 reps; all prompts cache-busted (no prefix reuse):

| Config | Cell | Input tokens/rep | Makespan mean | Aggregate input tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP8 | 128K c=64 | 8,226,496 | 232.5s | 35.4K |
| TP8 | 256K c=32 | 8,226,144 | 266.5s | 30.9K |
| TP8 | 512K c=16 | 8,354,496 | 344.3s | 24.3K |
| TP8 | 1M c=8 | 8,354,408 | 501.7s | 16.7K |
| DP8 | 1M c=2 | 2,088,602 | 93.3s | 23.8K |
| DP8 | 1M c=4 | 4,177,204 | 97.1s | 46.0K |
| DP8 | 1M c=8 | 8,354,408 | 172.1s | 50.0K |
| **DP8** | **1M c=16** | **16,708,816** | **267.3s** | **65.0K** |

DP8's aggregate uncached prefill throughput at 1M c=16 (65.0K input tok/s) is ~3.9x TP8's best 1M cell. TP8 1M c=16 is excluded (survivors-only under 600s timeouts, biased). These aggregates are provided for cross-report comparability; TTFT percentiles above remain the primary serving metric for this workload shape.

#### Mixed-workload cells (TP8)

4 scenarios × 3 reps, all 100% ok:

| Scenario | TTFT p50 | Wall p99 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1x1M + 8x8K (512 out) | 64.0s | 69.4s |
| 1x1M + 8x8K (64 out) | 64.0s | 67.2s |
| 2x512K + 8x8K (512 out) | 43.0s | 46.3s |
| 2x512K + 8x8K (64 out) | 43.0s | 48.3s |

Short 8K requests complete alongside long prefills; their TTFT is dominated by the long prefill duration, not added on top.

#### Prefix-cache warm-document showcase

One 1M-token Federalist document loaded as shared prefix, 5 sequential follow-up questions (`max_tokens=128`):

| Question | TTFT | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 (cold) | 66.3s | ok |
| Q2-Q5 (warm, median) | 3.0s | ok |

Cache speedup: 22x. First question under 70 seconds, every follow-up in ~3 seconds.

#### KV-eviction probe

Two distinct 1M-token documents loaded sequentially, then doc A resent (TP8, 21.4M-token KV budget; coexistence check, not a capacity measurement; theoretical bound ~20 at 21.4M tokens):

| Step | TTFT | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Doc A (cold) | 78.5s | ok, clean |
| Doc B (cold, different content) | 65.4s | ok, clean |
| Doc A (resend) | 3.2s | ok, clean (not evicted) |

At least 2 documents coexist in the 21.4M-token KV cache without eviction. The eviction boundary was not found; this probe verified coexistence only. Warm speedup on the resent document: 24.7x.

#### Mixed-workload scheduling experiment

Tested whether vLLM v0.25.0 scheduler knobs can fix short-request starvation beside a 1M prefill. Scenario: 1x 1M request + 8x 8K requests (max_tokens=64), 3 reps each.

| Config | Short 8K TTFT p50 | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline (default scheduler) | 64.0s | Short requests blocked behind 1M prefill |
| `--long-prefill-token-threshold 65536` | 63.9s | Flag accepted, no effect on short TTFT |
| `--scheduling-policy priority` + threshold + per-request priority (1M=0, 8K=10) | 63.8s | No effect; scheduler does not preempt running prefill |

**All negative.** None of the scheduler knobs available on vLLM v0.25.0 improve short-request TTFT in mixed-workload scenarios. `--max-num-partial-prefills > 1` raises `NotImplementedError("Concurrent Partial Prefill is not supported")`. Queue isolation (as recommended in V4-Pro #43753) remains the only viable approach on v0.25.0 stable.

### DSpark trade-off matrix

DSpark with matched flags (fp4 indexer, mega_moe, deepseek_v4 parsers), `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, real Federalist prose, 3 reps per cell:

| Cell | TPOT mean (streaming) | TPOT p50 (streaming) | TTFT mean | Per-request throughput (incl. TTFT) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8K c=1 | 4.6ms | 4.7ms | 5.8s | 10.5 tok/s |
| 8K c=2 | 6.8ms | 8.3ms | 0.4s | 78.8 tok/s |
| 8K c=3 | 7.8ms | 6.3ms | 0.5s | 62.1 tok/s |
| 8K c=4 | 64.2ms | 9.9ms | 2.0s | 10.5 tok/s |
| 8K c=6 | 63.7ms | 16.1ms | 1.6s | 11.3 tok/s |
| 8K c=8 | 32.5ms | 21.2ms | 1.3s | 19.1 tok/s |
| **1M c=1** | withdrawn* | withdrawn* | 65.7s | N/A** |

\* The streaming-TPOT values at this cell (0.25ms mean) are a burst-delivery measurement artifact, withdrawn to prevent out-of-context quotation; the valid decode-window measurement is 2.08ms (matched-util re-measurement below). ** Throughput not meaningful for a TTFT-dominated cell (65.7s prefill, ~64 output tokens). The 8K c=1 TTFT mean (5.8s vs 0.4s at c=2) includes a first-request cold-start; p50 was 0.26s.

**Streaming-TPOT measurement caveat (resolved by the matched-util re-measurement below).** The 0.25ms mean (0.24ms p50) above is streaming inter-arrival TPOT, and under 5-token speculation it is **not a valid per-token decode latency**: tokens arrive in bursts of up to 6, so the inter-arrival mean divides by the number of stream chunks (~96 for 512 tokens at max_tokens=512), not the number of tokens. The vanilla comparison was additionally unmatched (util 0.95 vs 0.85; vanilla 1M TPOT from a random-token-ID ladder). The matched-util re-measurement below re-measures at max_tokens=512 with decode-window arithmetic on a matched-util A/B, yielding a defensible **4.1x multiplier** at 1M c=1.

**Tail-latency collapse at c>=4**: the mean TPOT explodes (7.8ms at c=3 to 64.2ms at c=4) while p50 stays single-digit (6.3ms at c=3 to 9.9ms at c=4). The mean inflation is driven by straggler requests, not uniform degradation. Under the tested 8K TP8 workload, SLO-bound serving should switch DSpark off at c>=4; treat c>=4 with caution on other workloads until higher-concurrency long-context cells are measured. Regime rule (8K TP8): DSpark on for c=1-3 (interactive), off for c=4+ (batch throughput). This matches the recipes-page guidance ("low latency & small batch size") and the SGLang pattern of dropping MTP at saturation.

#### Matched-util decode-window re-measurement

The crossover table above uses streaming inter-arrival TPOT at `max_tokens=64`, which is not a valid per-token metric under speculative burst delivery (the 1M c=1 row is artifacted; see caveat above). This subsection re-measures DSpark decode speedup with a method that is valid: decode-window TPOT = `(wall - TTFT) / (completion_tokens - 1)`, at `max_tokens=512`, on a matched-util A/B (both legs at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.85`, identical cache-busted Federalist real-prose prompts, temperature=0, streaming, 3 reps per cell). `min_tokens=512` is set because the model naturally generates <15 tokens at 1M context before EOS.

| Cell | Leg | Decode-window TPOT (mean) | Decode window (mean) | Streaming TPOT (mean) | Stream chunks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1M c=1 | Vanilla 0.85 | 8.44ms | 4.31s | 8.97ms | ~482 |
| 1M c=1 | DSpark 0.85 | 2.08ms | 1.06s | 11.18ms | ~96 |
| 8K c=1 | Vanilla 0.85 | 7.82ms | 4.00s | 7.82ms | 512 |
| 8K c=1 | DSpark 0.85 | 4.97ms | 2.54s | 9.71ms | ~262 |

**Decode-window multiplier (matched 0.85/0.85 util):** 1M c=1 = **4.1x** (8.44/2.08); 8K c=1 = **1.6x** (7.82/4.97). The multiplier is context-dependent: at 1M, each verify pass is amortized over more attention computation; at 8K, the decode is cheaper and the draft-model overhead is proportionally larger.

**Streaming-artifact contrast (side-by-side):** DSpark streaming TPOT (11.18ms at 1M) is 5.4x higher than its decode-window TPOT (2.08ms), because 512 tokens arrive in ~96 stream chunks (5.3 tokens/chunk); the inter-arrival mean divides by ~95 instead of ~511. Vanilla streaming TPOT (8.97ms) closely matches its decode-window TPOT (8.44ms, 1.06x) because tokens arrive individually (482 chunks for 512 tokens). This demonstrates that streaming TPOT is not a valid per-token metric under speculative burst delivery; decode-window TPOT correctly accounts for the burst structure by dividing by the actual token count.

```python
def gpu_snapshot() -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    cmd = [
        "nvidia-smi",
        "--query-gpu=index,memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,pstate",
        "--format=csv,noheader,nounits",
    ]
    try:

    rows = []

        metric = name.split("{", 1)[0]
        if any(key in metric for key in ("num_requests", "gpu_cache_usage", "kv_cache", "request")):
            try:
                value: Any = float(raw_value)
            except ValueError:
                value = raw_value
            keep.setdefault(metric, []).append(value)
    return {"selected": keep}


def cleanliness(text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    non_ascii_count = sum(1 for ch in text if ord(ch) > 127)
    cjk_count = sum(1 for ch in text if "\u4e00" <= ch <= "\u9fff")
    de_count = text.count("\u7684")
    return {
        "text_len": len(text),
        "non_ascii_count": non_ascii_count,
        "non_ascii_ratio": (non_ascii_count / len(text)) if text else 0,
        "cjk_count": cjk_count,
        "ascii_clean": non_ascii_count == 0,
        "corruption_clean": cjk_count == 0 and de_count == 0,
        "clean": bool(text) and non_ascii_count == 0 and cjk_count == 0 and de_count == 0,
    }


def percentile(values: list[float], pct: float) -> float | None:
    if not values:
        return None
    ordered = sorted(values)
    idx = min(len(ordered) - 1, max(0, round((pct / 100.0) * (len(ordered) - 1))))
    return ordered[idx]


def build_base_prompt(context: str, federalist: str, variant: int, repeat: int = 0) -> str:
    cfg = CONTEXTS[context]
    n_reps = int(cfg["repeats"])
    ts = time.time_ns()
    parts = []
    for i in range(n_reps):
        parts.append(f"[Segment {repeat}-{variant}-{i}-{ts}]")
        parts.append(federalist)
    base = "\n\n".join(parts)
    return (
        "Continue the following public-domain prose in plain ASCII English.\n\n"
        f"{base}"
    )


def stream_completion(args: argparse.Namespace, spec: RequestSpec, prompt: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    url = f"{args.base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/completions"
    body = {
        "model": args.model,
        "prompt": prompt,
        "max_tokens": spec.max_tokens,
        "temperature": 0,
        "stream": True,
        "stream_options": {"include_usage": True},
    }
    timeout_s = int(CONTEXTS[spec.context]["timeout_s"])
    started = time.time()
    first_token = None
    last_token = None
    chunks = 0
    text_parts: list[str] = []
    usage = None
    error = None
    status_code = None
    try:
        with requests.post(url, json=body, stream=True, timeout=(30, timeout_s)) as resp:
            status_code = resp.status_code
            if resp.status_code >= 400:
                error = f"HTTP {resp.status_code}: {resp.text[:1000]}"
            else:
                for line in resp.iter_lines():
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    if line.startswith(b"data: "):
                        data = line[6:].strip()
                    else:
                        data = line.strip()
                    if data == b"[DONE]":
                        break
                    try:
                        obj = json.loads(data)
                    except json.JSONDecodeError:
                        continue
                    if obj.get("usage"):
                        usage = obj.get("usage")
                    for choice in obj.get("choices", []):
                        delta = choice.get("text") or ""
                        if delta:
                            now = time.time()
                            if first_token is None:
                                first_token = now
                            last_token = now
                            chunks += 1
                            text_parts.append(delta)
    except Exception as exc:
        error = repr(exc)
    finished = time.time()
    text = "".join(text_parts)
    clean = cleanliness(text)
    return {
        "label": spec.label,
        "role": spec.role,
        "context": spec.context,
        "max_tokens": spec.max_tokens,
        "prompt_chars": len(prompt),
        "status": "ok" if error is None else "error",
        "status_code": status_code,
        "error": error,
        "started_at_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(started)),
        "finished_at_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(finished)),
        "wall_sec": finished - started,
        "ttft_sec": (first_token - started) if first_token is not None else None,
        "decode_sec": (last_token - first_token) if first_token is not None and last_token is not None else None,
        "stream_chunks": chunks,
        "usage": usage,
        "cleanliness": clean,
        "text_first_240": text[:240],
        "text_last_240": text[-240:],
    }


def run_specs(args: argparse.Namespace, name: str, specs: list[RequestSpec], federalist: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    cell_dir = args.out_dir / name
    cell_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for spec in specs:
        (cell_dir / f"{spec.label}.request.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "label": spec.label,
                    "role": spec.role,
                    "context": spec.context,
                    "max_tokens": spec.max_tokens,
                    "delay_s": spec.delay_s,
                },
                indent=2,
            )
        )

    all_repeat_results = []
    for rep in range(1, args.repeats + 1):
        rep_name = f"rep{rep}" if args.repeats > 1 else "rep1"
        prompts = {
            spec.label: build_base_prompt(spec.context, federalist, idx, rep)
            for idx, spec in enumerate(specs, start=1)
        }
        print(f"=== {name}/{rep_name} start requests={len(specs)} ===", flush=True)
        before_gpu = gpu_snapshot()
        before_metrics = metrics_snapshot(args.base_url)
        start_wall = time.time()
        barrier = threading.Barrier(len(specs))

        def worker(spec: RequestSpec, _prompts: dict[str, str] = prompts) -> dict[str, Any]:
            barrier.wait()
            if spec.delay_s:
                time.sleep(spec.delay_s)
            return stream_completion(args, spec, _prompts[spec.label])

        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(specs)) as pool:
            rows = list(pool.map(worker, specs))

        end_wall = time.time()
        after_gpu = gpu_snapshot()
        after_metrics = metrics_snapshot(args.base_url)
        rep_result = {
            "rep": rep,
            "started_at_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(start_wall)),
            "finished_at_utc": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(end_wall)),
            "cell_wall_sec": end_wall - start_wall,
            "gpu_before": before_gpu,
            "gpu_after": after_gpu,
            "metrics_before": before_metrics,
            "metrics_after": after_metrics,
            "requests": rows,
            "summary": summarize_requests(rows),
        }
        (cell_dir / f"{rep_name}.result.json").write_text(json.dumps(rep_result, indent=2))
        all_repeat_results.append(rep_result)
        rep_summary = rep_result["summary"]
        print(
            f"{name}/{rep_name} done wall={rep_result['cell_wall_sec']:.1f}s "
            f"ok={rep_summary['ok']}/{rep_summary['requests']} "
            f"clean={rep_summary['clean']}/{rep_summary['requests']} "
            f"ttft_p50={rep_summary['ttft_p50_sec']} ttft_p99={rep_summary['ttft_p99_sec']} "
            f"wall_p50={rep_summary['wall_p50_sec']} wall_p99={rep_summary['wall_p99_sec']}",
            flush=True,
        )
        if rep_summary["ok"] < rep_summary["requests"]:
            print(f"  WARNING: {rep_summary['ok']}/{rep_summary['requests']} ok -- errors present", flush=True)

    cross_rep_rows = [row for rep in all_repeat_results for row in rep["requests"]]
    for row in cross_rep_rows:
        (cell_dir / f"{row['label']}.response_excerpt.txt").write_text(row.get("text_first_240", ""))
    cross_summary = summarize_requests(cross_rep_rows)
    result = {
        "name": name,
        "repeats": args.repeats,
        "all_reps": all_repeat_results,
        "summary": cross_summary,
    }
    (cell_dir / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    print(
        f"=== {name} ALL REPS done: "
        f"ok={cross_summary['ok']}/{cross_summary['requests']} "
        f"clean={cross_summary['clean']}/{cross_summary['requests']} "
        f"ttft_p50={cross_summary['ttft_p50_sec']} ttft_p99={cross_summary['ttft_p99_sec']} "
        f"wall_p50={cross_summary['wall_p50_sec']} wall_p99={cross_summary['wall_p99_sec']} ===",
        flush=True,
    )
    return result


def summarize_requests(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ok = [row for row in rows if row.get("status") == "ok"]
    clean = [row for row in ok if row.get("cleanliness", {}).get("clean")]
    ttfts = [row["ttft_sec"] for row in ok if row.get("ttft_sec") is not None]
    walls = [row["wall_sec"] for row in ok if row.get("wall_sec") is not None]
    decode = [row["decode_sec"] for row in ok if row.get("decode_sec") is not None]
    return {
        "requests": len(rows),
        "ok": len(ok),
        "clean": len(clean),
        "all_clean": len(rows) > 0 and len(clean) == len(rows),
        "ttft_mean_sec": statistics.mean(ttfts) if ttfts else None,
        "ttft_p50_sec": percentile(ttfts, 50),
        "ttft_p95_sec": percentile(ttfts, 95),
        "ttft_p99_sec": percentile(ttfts, 99),
        "wall_mean_sec": statistics.mean(walls) if walls else None,
        "wall_p50_sec": percentile(walls, 50),
        "wall_p95_sec": percentile(walls, 95),
        "wall_p99_sec": percentile(walls, 99),
        "decode_mean_sec": statistics.mean(decode) if decode else None,
        "errors": [row for row in rows if row.get("status") != "ok"],
    }


def make_concurrency_specs(cell: dict[str, Any]) -> list[RequestSpec]:
    return [
        RequestSpec(
            label=f"{cell['cell']}_r{i}",
            role="long",
            context=cell["context"],
            max_tokens=int(cell["max_tokens"]),
        )
        for i in range(1, int(cell["concurrency"]) + 1)
    ]


def make_mixed_specs(name: str) -> list[RequestSpec]:
    specs = []
    for group in MIXED_SCENARIOS[name]:
        for i in range(1, int(group["count"]) + 1):
            specs.append(
                RequestSpec(
                    label=f"{name}_{group['role']}_{group['context']}_{i}",
                    role=group["role"],
                    context=group["context"],
                    max_tokens=int(group["max_tokens"]),
                    delay_s=float(group["delay_s"]),
                )
            )
    return specs


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731")
    parser.add_argument("--haystack", type=Path, default=Path("/data/work/haystack-federalist.txt"))
    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=["concurrency", "mixed"], default="concurrency")
    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=3, help="Repeats per cell (for p50/p99 stability)")
    parser.add_argument("--only-cells", help="Comma-separated concurrency cell names")
    parser.add_argument("--mixed-scenarios", help="Comma-separated mixed scenarios")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    federalist = args.haystack.read_text()
    all_results = []
    if args.mode == "concurrency":
        cells = CONCURRENCY_CELLS
        if args.only_cells:
            wanted = {item.strip() for item in args.only_cells.split(",") if item.strip()}
            cells = [cell for cell in cells if cell["cell"] in wanted]
            if not cells:
                raise SystemExit(f"no cells selected by --only-cells={args.only_cells!r}")
        for idx, cell in enumerate(cells):
            if idx > 0:
                time.sleep(5)
            all_results.append(
                run_specs(args, cell["cell"], make_concurrency_specs(cell), federalist)
            )
    else:
        names = list(MIXED_SCENARIOS)
        if args.mixed_scenarios:
            wanted = {item.strip() for item in args.mixed_scenarios.split(",") if item.strip()}
            names = [name for name in names if name in wanted]
            if not names:
                raise SystemExit(f"no scenarios selected by --mixed-scenarios={args.mixed_scenarios!r}")
        for idx, name in enumerate(names):
            if idx > 0:
                time.sleep(5)
            all_results.append(run_specs(args, name, make_mixed_specs(name), federalist))

    summary = {
        "mode": args.mode,
        "repeats": args.repeats,
        "model": args.model,
        "results": [
            {
                "name": row["name"],
                **row["summary"],
            }
            for row in all_results
        ],
    }
    (args.out_dir / "t1-summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    (args.out_dir / "t1-results.json").write_text(json.dumps(all_results, indent=2))
    print("=== SUMMARY ===", flush=True)
    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), flush=True)
    return 0 if all(row["summary"]["all_clean"] for row in all_results) else 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

</details>

## Follow-ups in the comments (index)

items.title: [Perf][Kernel] Fused DSA indexer Top-k kernel (LiteTopk)
items.body:
## 📌 Description

Hi @youkaichao @WoosukKwon @mgoin @hmellor @njhill @Isotr0py @DarkLight1337, could you please take a look at this PR when you have a chance?

This PR introduces two complementary SM100 prefill optimizations for DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA):

- **LiteTopK** accelerates the indexer by fusing MQA scoring, online filtering, and TopK selection without materializing the `[num_q, seq_len]` score matrix.
- **LiteDSA** further accelerates the subsequent sparse-attention computation by packing multiple neighboring queries into one larger masked attention GEMM, reusing their heavily overlapping KV sets.

To the best of our knowledge, LiteTopk is the first Indexer-Topk implementation that avoids to store the score matrix, and LiteDSA is the first that converts multiple small per-token sparse-attention GEMMs into a grouped masked GEMM while preserving each query's original attend set. The corresponding paper is available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976).

**At 1M-token prefill, LiteTopK accelerates GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash by 1.29× and 1.08×, respectively. LiteDSA increases the end-to-end speedups to 1.40× and 1.25×, with no accuracy loss.**

Thanks to my collaborators Jianyang Gao ([@gaoj0017](https://github.com/gaoj0017)) from ETH Zurich, Peiqi Yin ([@yinpeiqi](https://github.com/yinpeiqi)) from CUHK, and Jiangneng Li ([@gravesprite](https://github.com/gravesprite)) from NTU.

### Motivation

DSA models such as **DeepSeek-V3.2/DeepSeek-V4**, **GLM-4.6/GLM-5.2**, and **LongCat-2.0** use a sparse-attention indexer during prefill. The current indexer computes an FP8 MQA score for every query/KV pair, materializes a `[num_q, seq_len]` matrix in HBM, and then runs a per-row TopK:

```python
logits = fp8_fp4_mqa_logits(...)        # materializes [num_q, seq_len] in HBM
ops.top_k_per_row_prefill(logits, ...)  # TopK over the materialized matrix
```

At 256K–1M context, this transient matrix is both large and expensive to write and read. After the indexer, the sparse-attention path launches many narrow per-token attention GEMMs. Neighboring queries usually select substantially overlapping KV positions, so those kernels repeatedly load and process much of the same KV data; at high tensor-parallel degrees, padding a small number of local heads to the kernel tile shape also wastes tensor-core work.

### LiteTopK: fused indexer scoring and TopK

LiteTopK avoids storing the score matrix:

1. Score KV tiles with FP8 MQA using tcgen05 UMMA.
2. Maintain an online **bucketed gate** with 256 histogram buckets and a self-calibrating threshold, discarding unlikely positions as scores are produced.
3. Run a compact TopK over the surviving candidates.

The candidate workspace is bounded independently of `seq_len`, replacing the dense `O(num_q × seq_len)` logits allocation and its extra HBM pass.

### LiteDSA: grouped masked sparse attention

LiteDSA targets the attention stage after TopK. If a rank owns `H` query heads, it groups `G = 128 / H` adjacent query tokens and packs their `G × H` real query/head rows into one 128-row tensor-core tile. For example, GLM-5.2 TP8 packs 16 neighboring tokens per attention call. Instead of running `G` small sparse GEMMs, LiteDSA performs one larger GEMM over the union of their selected KV positions.

The grouped computation remains query-exact:

1. **Union and KV reuse.** A GPU bitmap kernel deduplicates the group's TopK lists, emits the union in ascending order, and fuses logical-to-physical block-table conversion. Neighboring queries exhibit strong causal locality; the GLM path observes roughly 6–7× KV deduplication.
2. **Per-query masking.** A query-major membership bitmask records which union entries belong to each original query. The masked FP8 attention kernel applies this mask before softmax, so every query attends to exactly its original TopK set.
3. **Lower orchestration overhead.** Union, membership, and output buffers are persistent overwrite-write buffers. The union plan is version-cached and reused across layers that share the same indexer output, avoiding repeated allocation, clearing, and reconstruction.

DeepSeek-V4's C128A path uses the same packing principle with a structure-aware specialization. At TP8, 16 tokens × 8 real heads fill one 128-row tile instead of padding each token from 8 to 64 heads. Its compressed-prefix plus sliding-window structure is represented by exact per-query ranges over the group union; the ranges are derived directly from positions, cached per chunk, and avoid materializing the `[num_tokens, topk + window]` combined-index matrix. The measured union size is only 1.002× that of a single token.

In both paths, each union KV entry is loaded once for the group rather than repeatedly for every neighboring query. Unsupported shapes, CUDA Graph capture, non-SM100 devices, and other ineligible configurations transparently fall back to the existing attention path.

### Configuration

```bash
# LiteTopK indexer + existing sparse attention
VLLM_LITETOPK=1 VLLM_DSA_MODE=litetopk vllm serve <dsa-model> ...

# LiteTopK indexer + LiteDSA grouped sparse attention (supported FP8 sparse MLA path)
VLLM_LITETOPK=1 VLLM_DSA_MODE=litedsa vllm serve <dsa-model> ...

# DeepSeek-V4 C128A head-packed attention specialization
VLLM_DSV4_PACKED_ATTN=1 vllm serve <deepseek-v4-model> ...
```

## 🧪 Test Plan

> The kernel and end-to-end checks require an SM100 (B200) build and a DSA model.

```bash
# Build for SM100
uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto

# LiteDSA orchestration, buffer-lifetime, and DeepSeek-V4 packed-path tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
    tests/model_executor/layers/test_litedsa.py \
    tests/model_executor/layers/test_dsv4_packed_attn.py

# End-to-end long-context parity and performance
VLLM_LITETOPK=1 VLLM_DSA_MODE=litetopk \
    vllm serve <dsa-model> --max-model-len ...
VLLM_LITETOPK=1 VLLM_DSA_MODE=litedsa \
    vllm serve <dsa-model> --max-model-len ...

# Model evaluation for output parity
lm_eval --model vllm --model_args pretrained=<dsa-model>,...  # compare raw/litetopk/litedsa
```

## ✅ Test Results

### LiteTopK kernel-level validation

Hardware: NVIDIA B200 (SM100). Inputs: real GLM-5.2 indexer tensors, `Q=8192`, `top_k=2048`.

The dense FP32 logits buffer consumes **8 GiB at 256K, 16 GiB at 512K, 24 GiB at 768K, and 32 GiB at 1M**. LiteTopK removes this allocation.

| KV length | Dense (ms) | LiteTopK (ms) | Paired speedup median | Recall median |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 262,144 | 13.0469 | 10.6117 | 1.2266× | 99.9977% |
| 524,288 | 25.8997 | 20.4716 | 1.2652× | 99.9980% |
| 786,432 | 39.2471 | 30.0235 | 1.3084× | 99.9978% |
| 1,048,576 | 51.8106 | 40.1796 | 1.2929× | 99.9978% |

Recall rounds to **100.00%** at two decimal places across the tested settings.

### LiteDSA kernel-level validation

On captured DeepSeek-V4 C128A production data, head packing reduces sparse-attention kernel time from **6.565 ms to 0.839 ms (7.83×)**. Validation reports LSE max absolute error of `3e-6` and output relative error of `0.0025`.

### End-to-end 1M-token prefill

| Model | Input tokens | Dense (s) | LiteTopK (s) | LiteTopK speedup | LiteDSA (s) | LiteDSA speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GLM-5.2 TP8+EP8 | 1M | 152.89 | 118.66 | 1.29× | 109.14 | 1.40× |
| DeepSeek-V4 TP4+EP | 1M | 60.00 | 55.7 | 1.08× | 48.1 | 1.25× |

## Author

Ziqi Yin, Nanyang Technological University
